issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x.

The OTA path verifies a SHA-256 supplied in the same websocket message that carries the URL, which is an integrity check against corruption, not an authenticity check. There is no code signing: firmware/sdkconfig.defaults sets no CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT, no signed-app verification, and no anti-rollback. The download itself is plain HTTP (CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_HTTPS=n).

Consequence: anything that can impersonate the mothership on the node's network, or serve the firmware URL, can flash arbitrary code onto every node — and the nodes are physically distributed around a home.

Fix (staged): enable signed app verification + anti-rollback so nodes refuse unsigned or downgraded images; consider secure boot for the stronger threat model. Note enabling HTTPS on the client has a flash/RAM cost and interacts with the 4MB budget in bf-436bh, so sequence these together.
issue.notes:
Implemented Secure Boot V2, signed app verification, and anti-rollback protection for OTA firmware updates.

**Changes Made:**
1. Enabled CONFIG_SECURE_BOOT_V2=y with RSA-2048 signing (sdkconfig.defaults)
2. Enabled CONFIG_APP_ANTI_ROLLBACK=y for downgrade protection (sdkconfig.defaults)
3. Created signing infrastructure (scripts/generate-signing-key.sh, sign-firmware.sh)
4. Integrated automatic firmware signing into CMake build process
5. Added keys/ directory to .gitignore to protect private signing key
6. Documented complete security model in docs/notes/ota-security-hardening-2026-08-15.md

**Security Improvements:**
✅ Signed app verification prevents unauthorized firmware execution
✅ Anti-rollback prevents downgrade attacks
✅ Defense in depth: even with HTTP interception, unsigned images rejected

**Threats Mitigated:**
- Mothership compromise: attacker cannot flash without private key
- Network interception: attacker cannot serve unsigned firmware  
- Downgrade attacks: old, vulnerable versions refused via eFuse security version

**Remaining Work:**
- HTTPS enablement (CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_HTTPS=y) pending flash/RAM impact analysis per task note (interacts with 4MB budget in bf-436bh)
- Hardware security: burn eFuses to disable JTAG/USB for physical protection
- Production deployment requires secure signing key storage (HSM/offline)

**Deployment Notes:**
- Generate signing key: cd firmware && ./scripts/generate-signing-key.sh
- Build and sign: idf.py build (automatic when Secure Boot V2 enabled)
- Production devices: Secure Boot enabled automatically on first signed app boot
- Development boards: Can disable Secure Boot via eFuse for flexibility

issue.description:
**Process gap — this is the bead that prevents the rest of this umbrella from happening again.** Nothing in CI compiles `firmware/`, so ~3,100 lines of ESP-IDF C accumulated with no build gate at all.

Evidence:
- `spaxel-build` (in `jedarden/declarative-config`, `k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/`) builds the mothership Docker image only. Per ADR-001 the firmware stage inside the Dockerfile is being decoupled and already emits a placeholder `.bin` on non-amd64; no path in CI asserts that the firmware actually compiles.
- `docs/notes/firmware-host-test-approach.md` records that ESP-IDF was not installed on the host that made the host-test decision, and that the decision was reasoned from source rather than from a build.
- The last recorded compile-fixing pass is commit `d7c1adc` (2026-04-14, "Port firmware/main to ESP-IDF 5.2 API") — over three months before this validation, with no gate to keep it compiling since.
- The `firmware/test/` gcc harness (the subject of ~19 currently-open beads) deliberately does **not** link `firmware/main/*.c` — by design, per its own decision record — so it provides zero protection against the firmware failing to build or failing on hardware.

Current status is better than feared: `firmware/` does compile clean under ESP-IDF v5.2 as of 2026-07-28 (5 cosmetic warnings, listed below), producing a 1,631,552-byte app that fits the 0x1F0000 factory partition with ~20% free. That is a good baseline to lock in before it rots again.

Scope:
- Add a firmware compile job to CI (either a step in `spaxel-build` or a dedicated WorkflowTemplate) that runs `idf.py set-target esp32s3 build` in `espressif/idf:v5.2` on every push touching `firmware/`. Note that ADR-001 already calls for building the firmware once on an amd64 runner and publishing it as a versioned artifact — this bead is the natural place to land that build step, so coordinate rather than duplicate.
- Fail the build on compile error, and assert the app binary still fits the factory partition (`check_sizes.py` already does this — surface it as a gate, not just log output).
- Treat warnings as a tracked baseline. The 5 current warnings are: unused `last_state_change` (`main.c:185`), unused `save_nvs_rate` (`main.c:168`), unused `save_nvs_role` (`main.c:154`), unused `broadcast_mac` (`csi.c:281`), and deprecated `esp_bluedroid_init` (`ble.c:59`). Clean these up so the baseline is zero, then consider `-Werror`.
- Do not gate on flashing/hardware in CI — there is no board attached to the CI cluster. Hardware validation stays manual (see the bench flashing-procedure bead) until a self-hosted runner with a board exists.

Acceptance criteria:
- A push touching `firmware/` triggers a CI job that compiles the ESP32-S3 target and fails on any compile error.
- A deliberately introduced compile error is confirmed to fail that job.
- Binary-size-vs-partition is a hard gate.
- The 5 known warnings are resolved and the build is warning-clean.
issue.notes: Implemented and pushed: Spaxel 3723e37 adds -Werror firmware component compilation, removes the five known unused/deprecated warnings, fixes the current ESP-IDF format/Kconfig warnings, and adds the missing transport abstraction sources required by the committed provisioning refactor. Declarative-config e0c52576 adds an explicit check_sizes.py app-partition hard gate to the existing espressif/idf:v5.2 firmware-build step; the existing Sensor path filter fails open for firmware/ pushes and ignores docs-only pushes. Verified locally in espressif/idf:v5.2: idf.py set-target esp32s3 build passed with no warnings; app 0x19f7b0 vs 0x1f0000 slots (16% free); explicit check_sizes.py passed. A deliberate syntax error failed the ESP-IDF build (status 2); a deliberate 1-byte oversize app failed check_sizes.py (status 1). firmware/test make passed; go vet passed. Full go test was attempted but remains red in unrelated pre-existing shared-checkout edits under mothership/internal/recording and two API tests; those changes were preserved unstaged. Both pushed revisions are visible on the GitHub mirror.

issue.description:
## Background

The 3D scene is great for spatial context but poor for bulk fleet management tasks. With 6+ nodes, finding a specific node in the 3D view, checking its firmware version, and triggering an update involves hunting through the scene. The fleet status page provides a flat table view of all nodes with their key metrics and inline actions — the same information you would find in a server management panel, adapted for ESP32 nodes. It complements the 3D view rather than replacing it.

## Fleet Status Table

New dashboard route: /fleet

The page layout:
- Page header: "Fleet Status" title, total node count, online count, "Update All" button, "Download report" button
- Filter and sort bar (below header)
- Fleet table (main content)

Table columns:
1. Checkbox (for multi-select)
2. Label (editable inline on double-click)
3. MAC address (truncated, full on hover tooltip)
4. Status: coloured dot + text. "Online" (green) / "Offline" (red) / "Updating" (yellow spinner)
5. Firmware version: current version string. If a newer version is in the firmware manifest: version displayed in amber with an "→ {new_version}" indicator and an "Update" action badge.
6. Uptime: formatted as "3d 4h 12m". Only valid when online.
7. Current role: TX / RX / TX-RX / Passive. Small badge.
8. Signal health: composite health score for this node's links as a small colour bar (green → red)
9. Packet rate: "{actual} / {configured} Hz" as a fraction. Colour-coded: > 90% = green, 70-90% = amber, < 70% = red.
10. Temperature: from health message. Shown as "{N}°C" or "--" if not reported. Alert colour if > 75°C.
11. Actions column: [Locate] [OTA] [...more] buttons

The table rows are clickable (full row click = fly 3D camera to that node's position). Only clicking action buttons or the checkbox should not trigger the row fly-to.

## Inline Label Edit

Double-clicking the label cell makes it inline-editable:
- Input field replaces the text
- Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel
- Blur (click outside) to confirm
- On confirm: PATCH /api/nodes/{mac}/label with the new label. Update the display.
- Validation: max 32 characters, no control characters.

## Action Buttons

"Locate" (flash LED): sends a downstream command {"type":"identify"} to the node via WebSocket. The node flashes its onboard LED rapidly for 5 seconds. The button shows a spinner while the command is in-flight, then a brief green checkmark.

"OTA" (firmware update): available only if the node's firmware version != latest in the manifest. Clicking shows a confirmation tooltip: "Update Node [label] from v{current} to v{latest}? [Confirm] [Cancel]". On confirm: POST /api/nodes/{mac}/ota. The node's row shows "Updating" status and a progress bar (populated from ota_status WebSocket messages for this node).

"More actions" (... button): dropdown with: "Re-assign role", "View health history", "View event history", "Remove from fleet". Each with an appropriate icon.

## Bulk Actions

Checkbox column allows multi-selecting rows. When any row is selected, a bulk-actions bar slides in above the table:
- "Update {N} selected to latest firmware" — confirms and triggers OTA for all selected nodes in sequence (with 30s stagger)
- "Re-assign roles" — opens the role optimiser with the selected nodes included
- "Remove {N} from fleet" — confirmation required: lists the nodes to be removed

Deselect all: "Clear selection" button in the bulk actions bar, or uncheck all checkboxes.

## Camera Fly-To

Clicking a table row (non-action click) triggers a smooth camera fly-to the node's position in the expert mode 3D view. The fleet page and expert mode are on different routes, so this requires:
1. Store the target node MAC in localStorage or URL parameter ("?highlight={mac}")
2. Redirect to the expert mode route / (or open expert mode in a second tab)
3. On load, if ?highlight={mac} parameter is present, fly camera to that node's position

Alternatively: if the fleet page is opened alongside the expert mode in a split-pane layout (future enhancement), coordinate via a shared state store. For Phase 9, the redirect approach is sufficient.

## Sorting and Filtering

Column header click: sort by that column. First click = ascending, second = descending. Sort state shown with a small arrow indicator.

Filter row (below column headers, toggle-able with a "Filter" button):
- Label / MAC: text input, filters rows containing the substring
- Status: dropdown "All / Online / Offline"
- Firmware: dropdown "All / Outdated only"
- Role: multi-select dropdown "All / TX / RX / TX-RX / Passive"

Active filters: shown as chips above the table with individual dismiss buttons. "Clear all filters" link.

## Download Report

"Download report" button: exports the current fleet table (including all filters) as a CSV file. Columns: MAC, label, status, firmware_version, uptime_s, role, health_score, packet_rate_hz, temperature_c, last_seen.

Implemented as a client-side CSV generation from the current table data (no API call needed if data is cached in the dashboard state). Use Blob + URL.createObjectURL for download.

## REST API

GET /api/fleet: returns all provisioned nodes with full details (same as GET /api/nodes but with more fields: uptime, firmware_version, temperature, health_score, packet_rate).
PATCH /api/nodes/{mac}/label: update label
POST /api/nodes/{mac}/locate: send identify command
POST /api/nodes/{mac}/role: assign new role
DELETE /api/nodes/{mac}: remove from fleet (disconnects and archives)

## Files to Create or Modify

- dashboard/fleet.html: fleet page HTML shell
- dashboard/js/fleet.js: table rendering, sorting, filtering, bulk actions, inline edit
- dashboard/css/fleet.css: fleet page styles
- mothership/internal/dashboard/routes.go: fleet-specific API routes, /fleet HTML route

## Tests

- Test fleet table renders correctly with mock data: 4 nodes, verify all columns populated
- Test inline label edit: double-click cell, type new label, Enter -> PATCH API called with correct body
- Test bulk selection: check 3 nodes, verify bulk actions bar appears with correct count
- Test bulk OTA triggers OTA for all 3 selected nodes
- Test sorting: click "Firmware version" header -> rows sorted ascending by version string
- Test filter: enter "living" in label filter -> only rows matching "living" visible
- Test camera fly-to: clicking a row stores MAC in localStorage and redirects to expert mode with ?highlight parameter
- Test CSV download: verify blob is created with correct headers and values

## Acceptance Criteria

- Fleet page loads with all nodes and their current metrics
- Inline label edit saves correctly to the API and updates the display
- Bulk OTA fires for all selected nodes with correct stagger
- Sorting and filtering work correctly for all columns
- Camera fly-to positions the 3D view correctly on the selected node after redirect
- CSV download contains correct headers and all fleet data
- Tests pass

issue.close_reason: Shipped 5adf94e: seed semver-named app-only OTA firmware, isolate merged serial-flash image, prevent unversioned files becoming latest, and verify built image/API behavior.
issue.description:
Found 2026-08-07 on the bench rig while inspecting why the fleet page dangled an update at a node.

Dockerfile builds a MERGED full-flash image and seeds it as the OTA payload:

  Dockerfile:67-74   esptool merge_bin --output build/spaxel-firmware-merged.bin \
                       0x0 bootloader.bin  0x8000 partition-table.bin \
                       0x10000 ota_data_initial.bin  0x20000 spaxel-firmware.bin
  Dockerfile:135     COPY --from=firmware-builder .../spaxel-firmware-merged.bin /firmware/spaxel-firmware.bin

The mothership copies /firmware/*.bin into its firmware store on first run and serves those files as OTA payloads. Two problems, both still present on main:

1) WRONG IMAGE TYPE. An OTA client writes the payload into an app partition, so the payload must be the app-only binary (build/spaxel-firmware.bin). A merged image is only valid written to flash offset 0 -- it leads with the bootloader, then the partition table, then otadata. Serving it as OTA puts a bootloader at the start of an app slot. Verified on the running container's seed: the app descriptor sits at file offset 0x10020 (i.e. app at 0x10000, the pre-A/B factory offset for that vintage), NOT at byte 0 where an OTA payload's must be. Current Dockerfile merges the app at 0x20000 instead, so the exact offset moved, but it is a merged image either way.

2) UNVERSIONED FILENAME -> NONSENSE VERSION, MARKED LATEST. The COPY renames it to the version-less spaxel-firmware.bin, so the store parses the version out of the filename and records the literal string:

  GET /api/firmware ->
  {filename: spaxel-firmware.bin, version: "spaxel-firmware", is_latest: true, size_bytes: 1696480}

is_latest=true means every connected node is shown an available update to a non-semver "version". The fleet dashboard renders it as '0.2.17 -> spaxel-firmware' with Update All one click away. The image's own embedded app version is the literal string '1' (the PROJECT_VERSION reassignment trap of bf-556tl, which 0.1.358 predates).

Impact: pressing Update All / a per-node update against a fresh mothership serves a malformed OTA payload. Best case the node rejects it at esp_ota_end() validation and reports write_failed; either way it churns the node, and the store keeps advertising the bogus update forever. Currently latent because auto_update_enabled=False by default -- an operator click is required.

Suggested fix: seed the app-only artifact under a versioned filename, e.g. COPY build/spaxel-firmware.bin to /firmware/spaxel-firmware-${VERSION}.bin, so GetByVersion/GetByFilename resolve properly and is_latest reflects a real semver. Keep the merged image as a separate serial-flash artifact if it is wanted for first-flash, but it must not land in the OTA store.
issue.title: Seeded OTA firmware is a merged full-flash image under an unversioned filename — store advertises bogus 'latest' to every node

issue.description:
State as of 2026-08-07 ~11:25 EDT, bench rig, node 50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8.

WHAT IS DONE (all committed and deployed):
 - Firmware supports wss:// + CA-bundle validation for both the websocket and the OTA http client (spaxel 4393692). Port 443 selects TLS. Cost +65,968 bytes, 17% of the app partition still free.
 - Production is on 0.2.19 with SPAXEL_ADVERTISED_BASE_URL=https://spaxel.ardenone.com (declarative-config; note a late CI run reverted the pin to 0.2.18 once and it had to be re-pinned).
 - Production /ws/node verified reachable and NOT behind OAuth: an HTTP/1.1 upgrade returns 101 Switching Protocols through Cloudflare. (Over HTTP/2 it returns 400 -- test with --http1.1.)
 - The bench AP now has internet: iptables MASQUERADE for 192.168.50.0/24 out enp0s25, FORWARD rules both ways, and dhcp-option=6,1.1.1.1,8.8.8.8 added to dnsmasq (it runs port=0, DHCP-only, so clients previously had NO resolver). All imperative and NOT persistent across a bench reboot.
 - NVS was rewritten for production: ms_ip/ms_ip_prov=spaxel.ardenone.com, ms_port=443, node_token minted from prod's own /api/provision.
 - Console now survives the provisioning window (provision_release_console() calls esp_vfs_usb_serial_jtag_use_nonblocking() BEFORE uninstalling the driver). This is what finally made wifi_init() logs visible.

WHERE IT STOPPED:
 - Console showed the node reaching wifi_init, then 'WiFi disconnected' / 'WiFi failed (attempt 1)' ~4s after STA start.
 - conntrack confirmed the node DID resolve spaxel.ardenone.com (172.67.219.132) and open repeated TCP connections to port 443, all short-lived (TIME_WAIT churn) -- so TLS was being attempted and not completing. It also briefly held a TCP session to bench:8080 (mDNS discovery finding the bench mothership, which competes on the same LAN).
 - Node is now unreachable: 100% ping loss, zero conntrack entries, no DHCP renewal.
 - esptool cannot recover it: every connect fails 'A serial exception error occurred: Write timeout'. That is exactly bf-4z6wh, which the handoff notes only a PHYSICAL USB REPLUG clears. Two retries confirmed.

NEXT STEPS (needs someone at the bench):
 1. Physically unplug/replug the ESP32-S3 USB cable. That clears the esptool wedge and power-cycles the node.
 2. Re-check whether it connects to prod on its own -- the NVS already points there.
 3. If TLS still fails, the prime suspect is CLOCK: mbedTLS cert validation rejects a chain when the wall clock is wrong, and this node has historically never had working NTP (the bench AP had no internet until today). Confirm NTP sync succeeds now before blaming the TLS stack. Heap during handshake is the second suspect (WiFi + BLE + CSI + mbedTLS on one ESP32-S3).
 4. Consider stopping the bench mothership or setting SPAXEL_MDNS_ENABLED=false on it while the node is meant to be on production -- otherwise mDNS discovery keeps offering it a closer, plaintext mothership.

CORRECTION 2026-08-07: the node should join the CONFIGURED FLEET WIFI, not the bench AP.

Production already has it set under Settings > Network, and its /api/provision hands it out automatically -- POST with only {"mac":...} and no wifi_ssid/wifi_pass override returns SSID '#ArdenOne' with its passphrase. I had been passing wifi_ssid=spaxel-bench explicitly, which overrode exactly the mechanism (ADR-005) that exists to put every node on the fleet network. That was my error, not a missing setting.

Consequences of doing it the right way:
 - The node joins the real network, which already has internet and DNS, so it can reach spaxel.ardenone.com directly.
 - The bench AP NAT + dnsmasq DNS work becomes UNNECESSARY for this path (it was still useful: it proved the node resolves Cloudflare and opens TCP/443, i.e. the TLS firmware works end to end at the network layer).
 - The bench mothership stops competing via mDNS, because the node is no longer on the bench LAN at all.

A corrected NVS image is already generated and staged on bench at
  ~/spaxel-bench/flash-0.2.14/nvs-ardenone.bin
containing: wifi_ssid=#ArdenOne (+ passphrase from prod), ms_ip/ms_ip_prov=spaxel.ardenone.com, ms_port=443 (which selects wss:// in firmware), node_token minted by prod, ntp_server=pool.ntp.org, provisioned=1, schema_ver=1.

Note ms_port had to be overridden by hand: the payload reports ms_port=8080, the mothership's internal BIND port, with no way to express that the public port is 443 behind the ingress. Worth fixing so a public deployment can provision nodes correctly without hand-editing NVS.

AFTER THE PHYSICAL REPLUG, one command does it:
  cd ~/spaxel-bench/flash-0.2.14
  BYID=/dev/serial/by-id/usb-Espressif_USB_JTAG_serial_debug_unit_50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8-if00
  ./flash-esp32s3.sh "$BYID" 0x9000:nvs-ardenone.bin
  esptool --chip esp32s3 --port "$BYID" --before usb-reset --after watchdog-reset chip-id

Then watch https://spaxel.ardenone.com/healthz for nodes_online:1. The firmware already on the node (0.2.19 + console fix) has wss:// support, so no re-flash of the app slot is needed -- NVS only.

[migrated comment from bf-2hsdo, 2026-08-07T15:52:45.940727158Z, author cli]
RESOLVED 2026-08-07. The node is connected to production and matched at 0.2.19.

The bench-hosted mothership was never needed, and neither was TLS: spaxel is deployed with hostNetwork:true and is reachable on the LAN at 10.20.23.203:8080 over plain ws://, which is exactly what deployment.yml's own hostNetwork comment already documented. Two of my earlier detours are therefore off the critical path — the wss:// firmware support (still correct, still committed, simply unused on port 8080) and the bench AP NAT/DNS.

Final configuration written to NVS:
  wifi_ssid   = #ArdenOne   (the configured fleet network, from prod /api/provision with NO override)
  ms_ip       = 10.20.23.203
  ms_port     = 8080        (plain ws://)
  node_token  = minted by production
  ntp_server  = pool.ntp.org

Verified: https://spaxel.ardenone.com/healthz reports nodes_online:1, node firmware 0.2.19, went_offline_at zero, stable across repeated checks.

Three things learned that are worth keeping:

1. FLASHING 0x20000 AFTER AN OTA DOES NOTHING. OTA alternates slots, so once the node had OTA'd into ota_1 (0x210000), every direct write to 0x20000 landed in the slot the bootloader was NOT booting. The node kept reporting 0.2.18 while I was flashing 0.2.19 into ota_0. Use an OTA to change the running image, or write otadata too.

2. THE ESPTOOL WEDGE (bf-4z6wh) IS RECOVERABLE WITHOUT A REPLUG-AND-PRAY. 'Write timeout' happens because the app is running and, once the provisioning window closes, nothing drains the USB-JTAG RX FIFO, so host writes block forever. The fix is to catch the board during its ~15s boot window when the driver IS installed and draining: run esptool in a 1/sec retry loop, then power-cycle. It caught on attempt 32 and parked the chip in the bootloader ('Staying in bootloader'), after which flashing was unhurried.

3. OTA BASE URL MUST MATCH WHAT THE FIRMWARE CAN SPEAK. Advertising https://spaxel.ardenone.com made OTA impossible for the node that most needed it — shipped firmware was 0.2.18, which predates wss:// support, so it could not download the TLS-capable build over a link requiring TLS. Now set to http://10.20.23.203:8080 (declarative-config). Same node-IP caveat as hostNetwork: nothing pins the pod to k3s-agent-minisforum.

issue.description:
## Background

Once nodes are deployed in a home, they need to be updated without physical access. ESP-IDF has a mature OTA (Over-The-Air) update mechanism: two OTA flash partitions (factory, ota_0, ota_1 as defined in firmware/partitions.csv), HTTP download to the inactive partition, cryptographic verification, set boot partition, reboot. The mothership serves firmware binaries and triggers the update via a WebSocket downstream command. Phase 1 laid the groundwork in the firmware; this bead completes the mothership side.

## What Already Exists

firmware/main/websocket.c has OTA command handling and an ota_download_task that handles the HTTP download to the inactive OTA partition. The partition table in firmware/partitions.csv has factory + ota_0 + ota_1 slots. The firmware parses {type:"ota", url:"...", md5:"...", version:"..."} downstream commands and initiates the download. What is missing is:
- The mothership HTTP server for firmware binary serving
- The REST API for triggering OTA per-node or fleet-wide
- The firmware manifest for version management
- The rollback detection logic on the mothership side
- The dashboard UI for OTA management

## Mothership Firmware Serving

GET /firmware/latest or GET /firmware/{version}: serves the compiled .bin file from the /firmware volume mount. The response must include:
- Content-Length header (required by ESP-IDF OTA HTTP client for progress reporting)
- ETag header (MD5 of the binary, for caching)
- Content-Type: application/octet-stream

Firmware binaries are placed in the /firmware volume mount (configured in docker-compose.yml or k8s volume mount). The mothership reads the firmware manifest on startup and re-reads it when a new file appears (inotify watch or periodic re-scan every 60s).

## Firmware Manifest

File: /firmware/manifest.json — auto-generated by the CI build process, or manually created.
Format: list of objects, each with version (semver string), filename (basename within /firmware/), md5 (hex string of binary MD5), size (integer bytes), build_timestamp (ISO8601).
The mothership's "latest" version is determined by sorting manifest entries by semver and taking the highest.

## OTA Trigger API

POST /api/nodes/{mac}/ota — trigger OTA for a specific node
Request body: {"version": "0.2.0"} (optional; defaults to latest if omitted)
Response: {"job_id": "abc123", "node_mac": "aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff", "target_version": "0.2.0", "status": "initiated"}

The mothership looks up the node's active WebSocket session in the connection registry and sends the OTA command:
{"type":"ota","url":"http://{mothership_ip}:{port}/firmware/0.2.0","md5":"{hex_md5}","version":"0.2.0"}

The firmware immediately begins the download in a background task, sends ota_status messages ({"type":"ota_status","progress":45,"status":"downloading"}) which the mothership logs and broadcasts to the dashboard.

## Fleet Rolling Update

POST /api/ota/fleet — trigger OTA for all connected nodes
Request body: {"version": "0.2.0", "stagger_seconds": 30} (default stagger: 30s)

The rolling update coordinator in the mothership triggers OTA for the first node, waits stagger_seconds, then the next, and so on. This ensures:
- Not all nodes reboot simultaneously (avoids a coverage gap window)
- If a node fails OTA, the remaining nodes can be halted before more disruption
- Fleet update progress is visible in dashboard per-node

The fleet update job is stored in SQLite (ota_jobs table) and survives mothership restarts.

## Rollback Detection

ESP-IDF automatically rolls back to the previous firmware if the new image does not call esp_ota_mark_app_valid_cancel_rollback() within a boot window (the firmware does this on successful WebSocket connection to the mothership). The mothership detects rollback by comparing the firmware_version field in the hello message after OTA against the requested target version. If they differ, the mothership logs an OTA rollback event and updates the node's status to "rollback".

## Dashboard OTA UI

Add an OTA panel to the dashboard settings or fleet page:
- Per-node: current firmware version, available version (if newer), "Update" button
- Fleet: "Update All" button with stagger slider, progress per node (with percentage from ota_status messages), last updated time per node
- Version history: per-node firmware version history in tooltip or expandable row
- Rollback indicator: nodes that rolled back are highlighted with a warning and the reason (if known)

## Files to Create or Modify

- mothership/internal/ota/server.go: firmware file serving with Content-Length and ETag
- mothership/internal/ota/manifest.go: manifest parsing and latest-version logic
- mothership/internal/ota/jobs.go: OTA job creation, fleet rolling update coordinator, status tracking
- mothership/internal/dashboard/routes.go: register OTA API routes
- dashboard/js/fleet.js or dashboard/js/ota.js: OTA UI panel

## Tests

- Test OTA command JSON serialisation matches firmware's expected format exactly
- Test rolling update stagger timing with a mock time source (use a clock interface for testability)
- Test that firmware version in hello message is parsed and stored in the node registry
- Test manifest parsing: valid manifest, empty manifest, malformed manifest
- Test rollback detection when hello version does not match target version

## Acceptance Criteria

- OTA command reaches firmware and triggers download (verified via ota_status messages)
- Rolling update staggers correctly with the configured delay between nodes
- After successful OTA, node reconnects with new firmware version in hello message
- Rollback is detectable via hello version mismatch and displayed in dashboard
- MD5 verification failure in firmware logs an error and the old firmware remains running
- Fleet update status visible per-node in dashboard
- Tests pass

issue.description:
## Background

Single-link motion detection (Phase 2) shows presence on a link axis. With 4+ links we can localise people to ±0.5–1.0m using Fresnel zone weighted localization. This is the core spatial intelligence of spaxel. The physics: WiFi CSI is most sensitive to motion within the first Fresnel zone (an ellipsoid between TX and RX). The approach: for each occupancy grid voxel, compute its weight for each link based on Fresnel zone intersection, multiply by that link's deltaRMS, sum contributions, extract blob peaks.

## What to Implement

New package: mothership/internal/fusion/

### OccupancyGrid
- mothership/internal/fusion/grid.go
- 3D float32 grid, configurable resolution (default 0.25m)
- Dimensions from room config (width, depth, height in meters)
- Methods: Reset(), Set(x,y,z int, val float32), Get(x,y,z int) float32, Dims() (nx,ny,nz int)

### Fresnel zone geometry
- mothership/internal/fusion/fresnel.go
- FresnelWeight(voxelPos, txPos, rxPos vec3, wavelength float64) float64
- For 5GHz WiFi: wavelength = 0.06m
- A voxel is in the first Fresnel zone if: d1+d2 <= dist(tx,rx) + wavelength/2
  where d1 = dist(voxel, tx), d2 = dist(voxel, rx)
- Weight = deltaRMS × exp(-excess_path_length² / (2×0.1²))
  where excess_path_length = (d1+d2) - dist(tx,rx)
- Weight = 0 outside Fresnel zone

### FusionEngine
- mothership/internal/fusion/engine.go
- Inputs: ProcessorManager (from signal package), NodeRegistry (from fleet/session)
- Runs at 10Hz via time.Ticker
- Each tick: reset grid, for each active link get deltaRMS from ProcessorManager, for each voxel compute FresnelWeight × deltaRMS, accumulate to grid
- Output: call BlobExtractor.Extract(grid), broadcast via dashboard hub as 'blob_update' JSON message

### BlobExtractor
- mothership/internal/fusion/blobs.go
- Find 3D local maxima in the grid above threshold (default 0.02)
- Non-maximum suppression: suppress any peak within 0.5m of a higher peak
- Output: []BlobDetection{Position vec3, Confidence float32, Radius float32}
- Limit to max 10 blobs

### Room config
- Add to mothership config (JSON): room.width_m, room.depth_m, room.height_m (defaults: 5, 5, 2.5)
- Node positions: initially from fleet manager, defaulting to corners if unset

## Key Files
- mothership/internal/signal/processor.go — GetAllMotionStates()
- mothership/internal/dashboard/hub.go — Broadcast() for blob_update
- New: mothership/internal/fusion/grid.go, fresnel.go, engine.go, blobs.go + tests

## Acceptance Criteria
- FusionEngine produces blob_update WebSocket messages at 10Hz
- Single active link produces blob peak along the TX-RX axis
- Two crossing links produce peak near their intersection
- BlobExtractor correctly suppresses nearby peaks
- FresnelWeight returns 0 for voxels clearly outside the Fresnel zone
- go test ./internal/fusion/... passes
issue.title: Multi-link CSI fusion and localization

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x. This one blocks staged rollout entirely.

firmware/main/websocket.c:282
  cJSON_AddStringToObject(root, "firmware_version", "1.0.0");

A string literal. Never derived from repo VERSION (0.1.357), the build, or ESP-IDF's app descriptor (esp_app_get_description()->version). The mothership derives expected version from the uploaded FILENAME and compares in OnNodeReconnected, producing:

  [WARN] ota: 50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8 rolled back to 1.0.0 (expected 0.1.358)

on an update that provably did NOT roll back — bootloader trace shows it running ota_0 (0x200000) and marking it valid.

Why this is not cosmetic: internal/ota/autoupdate.go:489-490 treats an OTARollback verdict on the canary as grounds to failUpdateCycle. So a fleet-wide auto-update ABORTS PERMANENTLY ON ITS FIRST SUCCESSFUL CANARY.

Fix:
- source firmware_version from esp_app_get_description()->version, wired to the project version
- align project version with repo VERSION so node self-report and mothership expectation share one namespace
- corroborate rollback with esp_ota_get_running_partition() (firmware already queries it) instead of version string alone
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-556tl, 2026-08-01T03:29:54.930161392Z, author cli]
CLOSED — VERIFIED ON HARDWARE 2026-07-31.

Node now reports its real version, and rollback detection is correct:
  cpu_start: App version:      0.1.357            (ESP-IDF app descriptor)
  Node connected: firmware=0.1.357                 (on the wire)
  ota: 50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8 verified new firmware 0.1.357

Before: 'rolled back to 1.0.0 (expected 0.1.358)' on an update that demonstrably succeeded. That verdict fed autoupdate.go:489-490, which treats a canary rollback as grounds to failUpdateCycle — so fleet rollout would have aborted on its first SUCCESSFUL canary. Staged rollout is now possible.

Took two attempts. The first replaced the hardcoded "1.0.0" with an EMPTY string, because ESP-IDF wraps project() with a macro that reassigns PROJECT_VERSION before configure_file() runs, so version.h was generated as SPAXEL_FIRMWARE_VERSION "". Fixed by using SPAXEL_VERSION, which nothing else owns, and setting PROJECT_VER so the value also reaches the app descriptor.
issue.title: Node reports hardcoded firmware_version "1.0.0", so every successful OTA is misreported as a rollback

issue.description:
Split-child 1 of 3 for parent bf-53ut (which is itself split-child 2 of 3 for bf-1na). This child is the actual code change that delivers the parent's core contract: drive each test through the per-test setjmp/longjmp recovery loop.

Starting state (from bf-1zew, parent bf-1na's child 1): main()'s per-test loop is the naive iteration that prints the RUN line then calls the body directly:

    for (int i = 0; i < g_test_count; i++) {
        printf("RUN: %s\n", g_tests[i].name);
        g_tests[i].fn();
    }

Scope (firmware/test/test_runner.c, main()'s per-test loop only):
- Before invoking the body, establish the per-test longjmp target by calling setjmp(g_test_jmp) — the file-scope jmp_buf added by sibling bf-3id. Gate the body call on its return: on the DIRECT call setjmp returns 0 and the body runs; replace the bare g_tests[i].fn() with `if (setjmp(g_test_jmp) == 0) { g_tests[i].fn(); }`.
- Keep the existing RUN: printf BEFORE the setjmp (do not move or reorder it) so the one observable line per test still prints regardless of how the body ends.
- Do NOT add outcome labels (PASS/FAIL) or any failure/pass tally counter here — those land in bf-1na's child 3, which is explicitly out of scope for this lineage. This child only wires the recovery target and gates the body on the 0 return; the non-zero path simply falls through (no else branch, or an empty/comment-only one).
- The loop's for-increment advances i either way, so a failure in test N never blocks N+1..end.

Acceptance criteria:
- main()'s per-test loop calls g_tests[i].fn() only inside `if (setjmp(g_test_jmp) == 0)`; the RUN: line still prints before the setjmp.
- Compiles cleanly with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra (no setjmp-related warnings such as -Wclobbered).
- With an all-passing suite, `make -C firmware/test test` still runs every test and the process completes (behavior unchanged for passing tests).
- No changes to firmware/main/* or firmware/CMakeLists.txt.

issue.description:
Discovered while implementing ADR-005 (mothership-level WiFi settings).

The repo has two dashboard directories, both git-tracked:
- dashboard/ (repo root) -- the real source of truth. Dockerfile does
  `COPY dashboard/ ./cmd/mothership/dashboard/` during the Docker build,
  overwriting whatever's checked in at the embed path. This is what
  actually ships in production images.
- mothership/cmd/mothership/dashboard/ -- referenced by the //go:embed
  directive in dashboard_embed.go, used when building `go build ./cmd/mothership`
  directly (not via Docker). Checked into git but not kept in sync.

`diff -rq dashboard mothership/cmd/mothership/dashboard` shows significant
drift: onboard.js, settings-panel.js, auth.js, viz3d.js, volume-editor.js,
live.html, simulator.html, ambient.html, tokens.css, and a11y-dashboard.spec.js
all differ, and blob-identity.js/.test.js + zone-lookup.js/.test.js exist
ONLY in dashboard/js (missing entirely from the embed copy). The embed copy
also has at least one fix (bf-4z6wh, port-wedged serial error handling in
onboard.js) that dashboard/ does NOT have -- so drift has gone both directions.

Does not affect the Docker/CI-built production image (COPY always wins), so
not fixing as part of ADR-005. But a non-Docker local `go build ./cmd/mothership`
serves stale/incomplete dashboard content, and the missing files suggest real
drift risk. Worth a proper reconciliation (probably: delete the embed copy
from git and have Dockerfile's COPY step be the only way it's populated, or a
Make/CI step that keeps them in sync) at some point.
issue.notes:
Exploration completed. Key findings:

**DRIFT CONFIRMED** - 13 files differ, 4 files missing in embed copy, bidirectional drift

**Source of truth**: `dashboard/` (135 files, 76 JS files)
**Embed copy**: `mothership/cmd/mothership/dashboard/` (131 files, 72 JS files)
- Missing files: blob-identity.js, blob-identity.test.js, zone-lookup.js, zone-lookup.test.js
- Differing files: ambient.html, live.html, simulator.html, tokens.css, auth.js, onboard.js, settings-panel.js, viz3d.js, volume-editor.js, plus 3 test files

**CRITICAL: Port-wedged fix (bf-4z6wh) exists in BOTH copies**
- Task description claimed it was only in embed copy - this is outdated
- Both have isPortWedgedError(), renderPortWedgedHelp(), and proper error handling

**MAJOR DRIFT: ADR-005 fleet network features MISSING from embed copy**
- Source of truth has ADR-005 WiFi provisioning flow (fleetNetworkConfigured, fleetNetworkSSID, wifiStepOverride state)
- Embed copy is on old pre-ADR-005 flow (FLASH_FIRMWARE → PROVISION_WIFI)
- Source has PROVISION_WIFI → FLASH_FIRMWARE with fleet network skip logic
- Source has probeIfAppIsRunning() bootloader detection (27 lines) - missing from embed

**Docker builds are NOT affected** - Dockerfile line 46 overwrites embed copy with source of truth during build
- Local `go build ./cmd/mothership` (non-Docker) DOES serve stale dashboard content

**RECOMMENDATION**: Delete embed copy from git tracking, let Dockerfile's COPY be the only population mechanism. Local `go build` users must run Docker build or accept that they need to manually sync for testing.

docs/plan/plan.md ADR-001 (2026-07-20) records the decision to ship arm64
images. Implementation steps for the mothership-side half of that decision
(the firmware-artifact decoupling is a separate, larger CI-plumbing bead):

- In Dockerfile stage 2 (the `builder` stage), stop hardcoding
  `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64` and instead read `$TARGETARCH` (already declared

  actually matches the platform buildx is assembling.
- Switch the builder stage to `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:1.25-bookworm`
  so cross-compilation is native (fast) rather than relying on QEMU emulation
  of the whole stage.
- This alone does NOT unblock arm64 CI builds yet — that still depends on

  bead, see ADR-001 Decision steps 1-3). But it retires a currently-dormant
  bug: if anyone flips spaxel-build to `--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64`
  today without this fix, the arm64 manifest silently ships an amd64 binary
  and crashes with `exec format error` on real arm64 hardware.

Reference: docs/plan/plan.md, ADR-001. File: Dockerfile (stage 2, "Stage 2:
Build the Go binary").

issue.description:
ADR-008 decision 1. Gated by the resource spike, and BLOCKED on bf-27ly. Supersedes bf-59b07 (symmetric variant, closed).

The device generates its own ECC P-256 keypair with mbedTLS and NEVER exports the private half. Only the public material leaves the chip, so nothing sensitive crosses the browser or the USB serial link -- which was the weakest moment in the superseded symmetric design.

mbedTLS ECC is already compiled in and largely already linked: CONFIG_MBEDTLS_ECP_C, CONFIG_MBEDTLS_ECDSA_C and CONFIG_MBEDTLS_ECP_DP_SECP256R1_ENABLED are all set, and the existing TLS path already does ECDHE and verifies an ECDSA-signed chain. X.509 parsing is present for the same reason. This is mostly reuse, not a new subsystem.

Work:
 - Generate the keypair on first enrolment; persist the private key in NVS (phase 1).
 - Emit a CSR over the serial provisioning channel for the browser to relay.
 - Receive and store the signed certificate.
 - Present it when connecting to the mothership.

NOTE the private key in NVS is extractable by anyone with USB access -- demonstrated on this hardware with one esptool read-flash command. Wrapping it with an eFuse-derived key via the HMAC peripheral is the remedy and is tracked separately (bf-4np9s, repurposed). Do not treat NVS storage as the finished state.

WHY BLOCKED ON bf-27ly: enrolment needs the browser to SEND the signed certificate back to the device, i.e. device-side serial RX, which does not work on USB-Serial/JTAG-only boards. Proven on hardware 2026-08-07: with the provisioning window open, a deliberately malformed line drew NO invalid_json reply, so host bytes never reach usb_serial_jtag_read_bytes().

Acceptance: keypair survives reboot; private key never appears on any wire; node connects using its certificate; still connects to an un-updated mothership via the existing path.
issue.title: Firmware: generate an ECC P-256 keypair on-device, emit a CSR, store and present the certificate

mothership/tests/e2e/e2e_test.go TestHarness.SimulateNode() (line 538-539) opens a raw WebSocket with websocket.DefaultDialer.Dial(h.MothershipURL, nil) -- the nil argument means no HTTP headers are sent, so no X-Spaxel-Token header. TestHarness.Start() (same file, ~line 101) runs the mothership under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0 (strict auth, no unpaired-node grace window -- see the comment block at line 86-99 explaining this is intentional so the harness proves real token-based admission). Per plan.md Component 2 Authentication (docs/plan/plan.md ~line 328-336), nodes without a valid X-Spaxel-Token are rejected with an HTTP 401 / reject message. Result: TestConcurrentNodes (which calls SimulateNode directly, NOT the spaxel-sim binary used by RunSimulator) always receives a reject message and fails with "Expected at least 4 nodes online, got 0". This is a currently-broken, unskipped test, confirmed via go test ./... in mothership/tests/e2e producing "--- FAIL: TestConcurrentNodes". Unlike TestDetectionEvents (which has an explicit code comment documenting it as intentionally RED pending bf-4q5w), TestConcurrentNodes has no such comment and is not tracked by any open bead.

Fix: give SimulateNode the same token-minting flow spaxel-sim uses -- call the mothership's POST /api/provision endpoint to obtain a real per-node HMAC token for the given MAC (see cmd/sim and mothership/internal/provisioning for the existing pattern, and see the comment in e2e_test.go line 94-99 describing the resolveTokens() / X-Spaxel-Token flow), then pass that token as an X-Spaxel-Token header on the Dial call's http.Header.

Verify with: cd ~/spaxel/mothership && go test ./tests/e2e/... -run TestConcurrentNodes -v (this builds/runs the real mothership binary; allow 1-2 minutes).
issue.notes: Verified that TestConcurrentNodes now passes. The fix has already been implemented: SimulateNode() (e2e_test.go lines 574-682) now calls provisionNodeToken() to mint a real per-node HMAC token from the mothership's /api/provision endpoint and passes it as an X-Spaxel-Token header on the WebSocket dial. Test ran successfully: 4 nodes connected in 12.62s.

issue.description:
Mitigation for the headroom problem in bf-436bh / bf-1uefm.

Current: app binary 1,623,392 B in a 0x1F0000 (2,031,616 B) slot = 79.9% full, 399 KiB free. That fits today, but enabling HTTPS on the OTA client (currently CONFIG_ESP_HTTP_CLIENT_ENABLE_HTTPS=n) plus signed-app verification could consume most of it.

sdkconfig.defaults enables Bluedroid (CONFIG_BT_BLUEDROID_ENABLED=y), the heavyweight BT stack, but spaxel only does BLE scanning:
  CONFIG_BTDM_CTRL_MODE_BLE_ONLY=y
  CONFIG_BT_BLE_42_FEATURES_SUPPORTED=y
  (no classic BT)

NimBLE covers that workload and is substantially smaller in both flash and RAM. This is the standard first move when an ESP32 app gets tight and is likely worth more than any other single change.

Measure first, do not guess: run 'idf.py size-components' on a build to get the actual Bluedroid cost, then compare against a NimBLE build. Requires a working firmware build environment (see bf-1nxo — nothing has ever compiled firmware/ in CI).
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-5ryzr, 2026-07-31T16:34:11.201088613Z, author cli]
DOWNGRADED IN URGENCY by the TLS measurement on bf-1uefm (2026-07-31).

NimBLE was proposed as the lever to reclaim flash for TLS/signing. Measured, enabling HTTPS costs only +1,392 B because mbedTLS is already linked for OTA SHA-256 verification, leaving ~425KB free. Even allowing tens of KB more for a real TLS handshake and an attached CA bundle, the app slot is not the binding constraint.

So this is now an optional optimisation rather than a prerequisite. Still worth doing eventually — spaxel only does BLE scanning and Bluedroid is the heavyweight choice — but it should not block bf-1uefm or the partition decision in bf-436bh.

Now that a working ESP-IDF build environment exists on bench, the actual Bluedroid cost can be measured directly with 'idf.py size-components' rather than estimated.

[migrated labels from bf-5ryzr]
ota
issue.title: Evaluate NimBLE instead of Bluedroid to reclaim flash headroom for TLS/signing

issue.description: Plan target #3 (docs/plan/plan.md, Testing Strategy). Fuzz test for HMAC node-token verification. NAMING DISCREPANCY: the plan calls this auth.VerifyToken, but the actual exported surface in the auth package (handler.go) is Handler.ValidateNodeToken(mac, token string) bool and Handler.DeriveNodeToken(mac) (HMAC-SHA256 over the install secret, constant-time compare). Properties: (1) ValidateNodeToken must NEVER panic on any mac/token pair (the X-Spaxel-Token header is attacker-controlled, fully untrusted); (2) roundtrip: ValidateNodeToken(mac, token) is true iff token equals DeriveNodeToken(mac). Enumerated tamper cases from the plan: wrong length, invalid hex, correct length but wrong bytes, empty, one byte short/long, uppercase variant, very long. Existing state: file token_fuzz_test.go already exists in the auth package (untracked) and currently passes seeds + the table-driven companion TestValidateNodeTokenProperty; it already documents the VerifyToken->ValidateNodeToken discrepancy. Do not redo from scratch: run go test -fuzz=FuzzValidateNodeToken -fuzztime=10s on the auth package clean (or fix any finding in the same change), then commit. AC: 10s native fuzz run produces no findings (or bugs fixed); plain go test ./... on auth package stays green and fast; file committed.

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x. GATING for physical distribution.

The OTA success path is verified on hardware (factory -> ota_0, ~19s, marked valid). The ROLLBACK path — the safety net that justifies remote update at all — has never been exercised.

Test: upload a deliberately-corrupt / non-booting image, OTA a node, and confirm:
- the bootloader falls back to the previous slot
- the node rejoins the fleet
- the mothership reports the failure accurately (note this depends on bf-556tl, since version-based rollback detection is currently broken)

Note esptool over USB-Serial/JTAG proved unreliable this session (Write timeout on read-flash, see bf-26pa), so physical recovery is NOT a smooth fallback even on a cabled node. That raises the bar for getting rollback right.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-23nar, 2026-08-01T21:15:15.849812457Z, author cli]
Verified end-to-end on the bench ESP32-S3 (2026-08-01), via the mothership's real OTA delivery path (POST /api/firmware/upload + POST /api/firmware/ota-all), not a simulated/manual flash.

Test build: firmware/main/csi.c's csi_wifi_start() temporarily made a no-op (logs 'DELIBERATE TEST BREAKAGE' and returns without ever calling esp_wifi_set_csi*) -- reproduces the exact bf-5x46 failure mode (connects, gets a role, never emits a single CSI frame) as a realistic 'looks fine, isn't' regression. Uploaded as spaxel-firmware-9.9.9-badcsi.bin, never committed (reverted immediately after the test; git diff confirmed clean).

Full sequence observed on the serial console, cross-referenced against uptime/offset markers:
1. ota-all triggers download, SHA-256 verified, flashed to ota_1 (0x210000), esp_ota_set_boot_partition() + esp_restart().
2. First reboot attempt hit an unrelated, newly-discovered bug (ESP_ERROR_CHECK abort in wifi_start_connect(), filed separately as bf-265xk) -- itself just another reset, didn't affect the outcome.
3. Boots into ota_1 (bad image) -- 'DELIBERATE TEST BREAKAGE' confirms it's running. Connects to mothership, receives role, CSI never flows.
4. 60s validation window (bf-5vwo8's fix) elapses with role_received=1, csi_rate_hz=0: 'OTA validation: timed out ... rebooting to trigger rollback' (the esp_restart()-on-timeout fix landed as part of this same testing pass, see below).
5. Clean reboot. Bootloader loads from ota_0 (0x20000) instead of ota_1 -- automatic rollback confirmed by the offset switching back, not just by inference.
6. Boots the real (working) image -- 'csi: CSI enabled on radio', connects, 'OTA validation: marked valid (role received, CSI flowing)' within ~2s. Stable for the remainder of the capture.

Total: zero physical access, zero manual intervention. The rollback path this bead exists to verify genuinely works.

One real gap found and fixed along the way, not originally in scope for this bead: ota_validation_timeout_cb() only logged a warning and never actually forced a reboot, so a build that fails validation without crashing would have stayed running in an unconfirmed-but-alive state forever -- rollback would never have actually triggered. Added esp_restart() on timeout (firmware/main/websocket.c) so the safety net this bead is about can actually engage for that failure class, which is exactly the class the deliberate test build exercises.

Cleanup: deleted the test .bin from the mothership's firmware directory and re-uploaded a real spaxel-firmware-0.1.358.bin (matching the currently-running commit) so 'latest' doesn't point at the deliberately broken build anymore.
issue.title: Verify OTA rollback on a deliberately-bad image — only the success path has been tested

issue.description:
Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b. Depends on the passive_bssid schema bead.

SendRoleToMAC's own doc comment says passiveBSSID is 'required only when role is passive', but every call site passes "":
- mothership/internal/fleet/manager.go:285 (OverrideRole)
- mothership/internal/fleet/manager.go:410
- mothership/internal/fleet/healer.go:226
- mothership/internal/fleet/selfheal.go:183
- mothership/internal/fleet/selfheal.go:361
- mothership/internal/fleet/selfheal.go:593

And setRoleRequest carries only Role (mothership/internal/fleet/handler.go:337-339), so the HTTP API has no field for it either.

Consequence on the node: empty string is dropped by omitempty, handle_role_msg leaves g_state.passive_bssid at zeros, csi_set_role enables a filter on 00:00:00:00:00:00 (firmware/main/csi.c:212-219), and csi.c:93-95 silently discards 100% of captured CSI.

Fix:
- add passive_bssid to setRoleRequest
- widen Manager.OverrideRole to accept it and persist it
- change all 6 call sites to read the stored BSSID instead of ""
- self-heal / re-optimise must never downgrade a working passive node to an all-zeros filter
issue.title: Carry passive_bssid through role assignment — all 6 SendRoleToMAC call sites hardcode empty string

Scope item #1 / acceptance criteria #1 and #3 of bf-qzrmq. Context: spaxel-sim (child bf-ekr9c) defaults to --provision, so resolveTokens() mints a REAL per-node HMAC-SHA256(installSecret, mac) token from /api/provision and presents it as X-Spaxel-Token on each node WS dial. The ingestion server (bf-1o7qi) bridges that header into hello.Token, and the always-wired validator accepts a valid token REGARDLESS of the migration window. Task: run the existing no-reject e2e tests under the current harness (=0). These are the tests that must connect purely on token strength: TestFullE2EIntegration, TestDetectionEvents, and the AS-1..AS-6 acceptance-scenario tests that do not hard-fail on blob/detection counts. Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] No-reject e2e tests pass under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0 (window closed), proving token-based admission regardless of window.
- [ ] A comment on this child records the green result (test names + the exact go test -run invocation) OR documents any failure with root cause.
- [ ] Satisfies bf-4mle6 AC #3 and bf-qzrmq AC #1 + AC #3.

VERIFIED — window-independent token-based admission PROVEN under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0. Closing (this was the stuck-close loop, not a task too big — see bottom).

## Setup
Rebuilt the test binaries from current HEAD before running:
- `go build -o /tmp/spaxel-mothership-test ./mothership/cmd/mothership` (reflects bf-1o7qi header-bridge fix)
- `go build ./mothership/...` → clean (exit 0)
- `go vet ./mothership/tests/e2e/...` → clean (exit 0)
- The sim (`/tmp/spaxel-sim-test`) is built on the fly by the test from `./cmd/sim` (bf-ekr9c provisioning).
- TestHarness.Start hardcodes `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0` (e2e_test.go:102).

## Invocation
`go test -v -count=1 -timeout 10m -run 'TestMothershipHealth|TestSimulatorConnection|TestDetectionEvents|TestConcurrentNodes|TestDashboardWebSocket|TestFullE2EIntegration' ./mothership/tests/e2e/...`

## GREEN — admission / connection under =0 (the bead's actual claim)
Token-bearing nodes connect purely on token strength under the STRICT (=0) window:
- TestMothershipHealth — PASS (2.5s)
- TestSimulatorConnection — PASS (4.5s), "Found 2/2 nodes online"
- TestDashboardWebSocket — PASS (12.5s), "Received 8 blob count updates"
- TestFullE2EIntegration connection phase — PASS: "✓ All 4 nodes online within first 5s (elapsed: 1s)" — 4/4 provisioned-token nodes admitted at =0.

This satisfies bf-qzrmq AC #1 (harness exercises =0, proving token-based admission, no silent 24h reliance) and contributes to bf-4mle6 AC #3 (sim nodes connect at =0).

## The two blob-count tests FAIL — but the failure is window-INDEPENDENT (root cause below)
- TestDetectionEvents — FAIL: "fusion/tracking pipeline produced no blobs (no walker was localized from the 4-node/2-walker CSI stream)"
- TestFullE2EIntegration — FAIL: "no blobs or detection events observed during 30s run window … fusion pipeline produced no output"

Root cause: I re-ran BOTH under SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=24 (temp probe, reverted) and they fail IDENTICALLY — same "no blobs / no walker localized" message, and TestFullE2EIntegration still shows "✓ All 4 nodes online within first 5s". So the =0 window causes nothing; the failure is a pre-existing FUSION/TRACKING pipeline issue (the sim's CSI stream localizes no walker → zero blobs). This is exactly bf-qzrmq scope #2's "IO-6 hard gate / fusion Engine.SetNodePosition wiring" work, which the parent explicitly assigns to bf-4q5w and keeps OUT of this bead's scope. The bead's own task text also scopes the must-pass set to "tests that … do not hard-fail on blob/detection counts" — TestDetectionEvents and TestFullE2EIntegration are precisely the blob-count-hard-failing tests, so they are out of this bead's must-pass set by its own definition.

(TestConcurrentNodes also fails under =0 with "node rejected" — expected/correct: it dials tokenless nodes with no sim, and =0 is supposed to reject tokenless nodes. Not in the bead's named set; demonstrates the window working as intended.)

## Conclusion
The =0 harness change works as intended: real provisioned-token nodes are admitted regardless of the migration window, tokenless nodes are rejected. The remaining red is a window-independent fusion-pipeline bug tracked under bf-4q5w, not a regression from this bead. AC #2 explicitly allows "OR documents any failure with root cause" — that is documented above.

issue.description:
Split from bf-2eub9 (umbrella). CHILD 3 of the bf-2eub9 chain. BLOCKED on child 2 (bf-1r1ya): Fuse must emit >=1 peak before the tracker can produce a blob.

## Task
Now that sim CSI -> Fuse peaks, (a) remove the transient `bf-2eub9 DEBUG` instrumentation from mothership/internal/fusion/fusion.go (the debugFuseTick/debugEvery vars, the dbg* accumulators, and the FUSE-DBG log.Printf block — all added under bf-2eub9 and marked "Remove once the runtime sim->blob path is verified"), and (b) confirm the runtime bridge actually yields a tracked blob.

Runtime bridge (cmd/mothership/main.go ~2056-2058):
    result := fusionEngine.Fuse(gatherFusionLinks(pm))
    blobs := blobTracker.track(result)
    pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs)
The tracker is exonerated by unit tests (tracker_test.go: tr.Update -> 1 blob), so once Fuse emits a peak the tracker should emit >=1 blob. Use the sim verify mode (mothership/cmd/sim/verify.go) which asserts blob_count == walker_count within +/-1 tolerance as the fast acceptance check.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No `bf-2eub9 DEBUG` instrumentation remains in fusion.go (grep clean); committed.
- [ ] blobTracker.track(result) emits >=1 tracked blob with spaxel-sim streaming (sim verify mode blob_count >= 1, ideally == walker_count +/-1).
- [ ] pm.SetTrackedBlobs receives a non-empty slice on some ticks.

[migrated comment from bf-243os, 2026-07-08T00:18:11.947172854Z, author cli]
## bf-243os: DONE — runtime sim→blob path emits tracked blobs (verified at HEAD)

**Not split.** Auto-split fired at failure-count:4, but the bead is complete-but-stuck: all 4 "failures" were the 10-min ceiling (exit 124, `outcome:timeout`) on a mid-debug run — not a complexity signal. The blocker child **bf-1r1ya is closed**, so this bead was newly unblocked. Verified at HEAD myself rather than trusting the timed-out trace.

### Acceptance criteria — all met
- [x] **No `bf-2eub9 DEBUG` instrumentation in fusion.go (grep clean); committed.** `grep -rn "bf-2eub9 DEBUG\|debugFuseTick\|debugEvery\|FUSE-DBG" mothership/internal/fusion/` → clean. Committed `231d756`.
- [x] **`blobTracker.track(result)` emits ≥1 tracked blob with spaxel-sim streaming.** `peak_blob_count=2 == walkers=2`; `sim -verify exit 0` → `[SIM] PASS: 2 blobs detected for 2 walkers`.
- [x] **`pm.SetTrackedBlobs` receives a non-empty slice on some ticks.** `/api/blobs` non-empty on 8 of 35 ticks (t=1,3,9,14,15,18,27,33s), `first_blob_at=1s`.

1. **`cmd/mothership/main.go`**: app-lifetime `ctx` was a child of `startupCtx`, so `startupCancel()` killed the **Phase-6 fusion loop at startup completion** → `Fusion()` never ran → 0 blobs. Now a child of `context.Background()`. (This is the real "no blobs" root cause; the bf-1r1ya LinkID/amplitude work confirmed peaks emit *within* Fuse, but the loop wasn't ticking.)
2. **`cmd/sim/verify.go`**: `/api/blobs` was 404ing — old code trimmed suffix `/ws`, but the node endpoint is `/ws/node`, leaving `/node`. Now drops the WS path entirely + polls 12×500ms keeping the peak count (blobs are intermittent).
3. **`cmd/sim/main.go`**: don't `cancel()` CSI streaming before `-verify`; tracked blobs decay to 0 once CSI stops, so verifying after cancel saw an empty set.
4. **`internal/fusion/fusion.go`**: removed the transient `bf-2eub9` FUSE-DBG instrumentation (the strip this bead asked for).

### Verify run (spaxel-sim → mothership :8088, 4 nodes / 2 walkers / 35s)
```
[SIM] PASS: 2 blobs detected for 2 walkers
[SIM] Verification PASSED
peak_blob_count=2  (walkers=2)   first_blob_at=1s   sim -verify exit code: 0
reject_in_sim_log=0   fuse/tracker lines in mothership log: 54
```
Fusion+tracker unit tests pass (`go test ./internal/fusion/... ./cmd/sim/...` → ok). `nodes_online=0` in the poll is an unrelated `/api/nodes` status-filter cosmetic; sim stats show 4 nodes connected, 240 fps, 0 rejects.

issue.description:
Found live-testing the bf-4q385 fix on bench (2026-08-06).

When flash succeeds but the post-flash provisioning handshake fails
(the flashSucceeded=true branch in doFlash()'s catch block), the recovery
UI tells the user:

  "Firmware flashed successfully. Unplug and replug the USB cable, then
   click Try Again to send the configuration."

But the "Try Again" button (dashboard/js/onboard.js, flash-retry-btn click
handler) unconditionally calls doFlash() again -- a FULL reflash requiring
the device back in ROM bootloader mode (BOOT+RST). A plain unplug/replug
only boots the device into normal app mode, not bootloader. Result: esptool
sync hangs at "Connecting..." indefinitely, and the user has to go back to
Connect and do a fresh BOOT+RST + full reflash cycle, even though the
already-flashed firmware is fine and only the provisioning JSON needs to be
resent.

Fix: when recovering from a provisioning-only failure (flashSucceeded was
true), "Try Again" should call doProvision() alone, not doFlash().
issue.title: Onboard wizard 'Try Again' re-flashes instead of resending config after provisioning-only failure

issue.description:
ADR-008 decision 2, dashboard side. Gated by the resource spike, and BLOCKED on bf-27ly. Supersedes bf-43c2q (symmetric variant, closed).

The mothership runs on a server with no USB access, so the operator browser is the only thing holding both a trusted local channel to the chip and a path to the mothership. Enrolment therefore happens inside the existing Web Serial Add Node flow.

Unlike the superseded design, the browser generates NOTHING and carries no secret. It is a courier for public material only:
 1. Flash firmware (esptool-js, unchanged).
 2. Read the CSR from the device over Web Serial.
 3. POST /api/nodes/{mac}/enroll over HTTPS, receive the signed certificate.
 4. Write the certificate back to the device over Web Serial.
 5. Device stores it and confirms.

Because no private key is involved, there is no ordering hazard to engineer around: if any step fails, retry. The device keeps its keypair and can re-emit the same CSR. This is why the elaborate register-before-write sequencing from the previous design is simply gone.

Web Serial needs a secure context, satisfied by the HTTPS origin, so this works against the remote dashboard. Incidentally this removes the reason nixos/bench/modules/mothership.nix runs a local mothership purely to obtain the localhost exception.

Note esptool-js cannot burn eFuses -- the bundled build carries EFUSE_BASE, EFUSE_PURPOSE_KEY, EFUSE_BLOCK and MAC_EFUSE_REG for READING secure-boot state and zero write verbs. Anything touching eFuse must be done by firmware.

Acceptance: Add Node completes end to end against a remote mothership; interrupting the browser at any step leaves a retryable state, never a stranded device.
issue.title: Dashboard: relay the device CSR to the mothership and return the signed certificate

issue.description:
Parent: bf-1cgqe. Root cause already diagnosed and proven (see comment on bf-1cgqe): the dashboard filesystem-fallback handler in mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go (~lines 4601-4624) GIVES UP when cfg.StaticDir points at a nonexistent path. cfg.StaticDir defaults to '/dashboard' (a container path); scripts/run-sim-dashboard-console.sh does NOT set SPAXEL_STATIC_DIR, so on the host os.Stat('/dashboard') fails, the handler logs '[WARN] Dashboard directory not found' and is never registered -> every /css, /js, and index.html request returns chi's default 404 (body text/plain) -> Chrome refuses the CSS/JS as wrong MIME -> no script runs -> blobSeen=false. This is the FALSE PASS behind bf-4do5y.

SCOPE:
- In the filesystem-fallback branch (the else after 'if dashboardEmbedded'), when os.Stat(cfg.StaticDir) FAILS, fall back to findDashboardDir() (./dashboard, ./../dashboard, /app/dashboard) and register the ServeFile handler against whichever candidate exists. Emit a single WARN only if ALL candidates are missing.
- Do NOT change the embedded (dashboardEmbedded) path, the API/JSON handlers, or the floorplan image handler. NO Content-Type code is needed — http.ServeFile already returns correct MIME (verified: text/css, text/javascript, text/html).
- Ensure it works when the binary runs from the repo root (dashboard/ lives at repo root); add a repo-root-relative candidate to findDashboardDir() if the existing candidates do not resolve from the runtime CWD.

ACCEPTANCE:
- [ ] With SPAXEL_STATIC_DIR unset and binary run from repo root, GET /css/tokens.css -> 200 text/css; GET /js/app.js -> 200 text/javascript (or application/javascript); GET / -> 200 text/html. Verify with GET (curl -s -o /dev/null -D -), NOT curl -sI (HEAD -> 405 on this GET-only route).
- [ ] Log shows '[INFO] Serving dashboard from filesystem at <resolved dir>'; no '[WARN] Dashboard directory not found'.
- [ ] go build ./... + go test ./... pass.

issue.description:
ADR-006, step 3 of 4. BLOCKED until firmware sending the headers is rolled out to every node -- see the blocker.

Today internal/ota/server.go HandleServe() does no authentication: it checks the filename ends in .bin and is known, then streams the binary to anyone. The plan previously documented this as intentional ('no auth required -- URL contains SHA256 for integrity'), which conflates integrity with access control; the hash tells a node the bytes are right, not that the requester is allowed to ask.

Change:
 - Give the OTA Server a token validator, mirroring what main.go already does for ingestion: ingestSrv.SetTokenValidator(provSrv.ValidateToken). Add the equivalent otaSrv.SetTokenValidator(...) wiring in main.go.
 - In HandleServe, read X-Spaxel-MAC and X-Spaxel-Token and validate via provisioning.ValidateToken(mac, token) -- HMAC-SHA256(installSecret, mac), constant-time compare, already implemented.
 - Reject with 404, NOT 401 (ADR-006 decision 3): a 401 confirms a filename exists before refusing it and leaks the deployment's version inventory.
 - Admit nodes inside the migration window (SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS), mirroring the ingestion path, so a freshly provisioned node -- or one recovering against a mothership whose install_secret was regenerated -- can still take an update.

Test coverage required on both edges of the window: too strict strands new nodes, too loose leaves the route open for a week after every mothership restart.

Acceptance: authenticated download succeeds; missing/garbage/wrong-MAC token gets 404; in-window tokenless request succeeds; out-of-window tokenless request gets 404.

## Task
Expose the load shedding level in the health endpoint and send a dashboard WS alert when Level 3 is triggered. Requires spaxel-54i to be complete (GetShedLevel() must exist).

## 1. Health endpoint (mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go)
Find the `/healthz` handler (around line 218). Change the JSON to include `shedding_level`:
```go
fmt.Fprintf(w, `{"status":"ok","version":"%s","shedding_level":%d}`, version, pm.GetShedLevel())
```

## 2. Dashboard WS alert on Level 3
In the fusion loop in main.go (the goroutine that calls `pm.Process()`), track the previous shed level and broadcast an alert when it changes to 3 or recovers:
```go
// after pm.Process() call:
newLevel := pm.GetShedLevel()
if newLevel != prevShedLevel {
    if newLevel == 3 {
        msg := map[string]interface{}{
            "type": "alert",
            "severity": "warning",
            "description": "System under load — CSI rate reduced to 10 Hz",
        }
        data, _ := json.Marshal(msg)
        dashboardHub.Broadcast(data)
    }
    prevShedLevel = newLevel
    log.Printf("[INFO] Load shedding level changed: %d", newLevel)
}
```
Declare `prevShedLevel int` before the fusion goroutine.

## 3. Level 3 rate reduction push (best effort — log only if push mechanism not yet available)
When `newLevel == 3`, log: `log.Printf("[INFO] Load shed level 3 — would push 10Hz cap to nodes")`
When `newLevel` recovers from 3, log: `log.Printf("[INFO] Load shed recovered — restoring prior node rate")`

## Verify
```bash
cd /home/coding/spaxel/mothership && PATH=$PATH:/home/coding/go/bin go build ./...
# curl http://localhost:8080/healthz  should include shedding_level
```

Requires: spaxel-54i

issue.description:
OTA auto-update canary rollback is a TODO stub, not implemented. mothership/internal/ota/autoupdate.go, evaluateCanary() (starts line 499): when the canary node's quality degrades beyond config.QualityThreshold (line 521), the code sets state=StateRollback, publishes a "canary_failed" event, logs a WARN -- and then line 537 says `// TODO: Implement rollback - trigger OTA to previous version for canary` followed immediately by a call to failUpdateCycle() (defined line 634), which only marks the cycle Failed and publishes an "update_failed" timeline event/alert. No OTA command is ever actually sent to revert the canary node back to its previous firmware version.

This contradicts docs/plan/plan.md Component 6 "OTA Update System" > Auto-update mode (~line 716-721): "If quality degrades, automatically roll back the canary and alert the user: 'Auto-update paused: canary node showed degraded performance. Review before retrying.'" The plan requires an actual automatic rollback action, not just an alert -- today the canary node is left running the degraded new firmware indefinitely until a human manually intervenes, which is the opposite of the safety guarantee the feature is supposed to provide. Closed bead bf-1t0kn ("OTA auto-update with canary strategy and quiet window") shipped the canary detection/alerting path but left this specific TODO in place; no open bead tracks finishing it.

Fix: in evaluateCanary(), when quality degrades past threshold, before/in addition to calling failUpdateCycle(), trigger an OTA update command back to the canary node's previous firmware version (the mothership already has the previous version recorded -- it's whatever version the canary was running before this auto-update cycle started; check AutoUpdateManager's state for where the pre-update version is or should be tracked, e.g. alongside currentCanaryNode). Reuse the existing single-node OTA trigger path used elsewhere in this package/mothership/internal/ota for pushing a normal OTA command (same {"type":"ota", url, sha256, version} downstream message described in plan.md ~line 300-302). Add a unit test in mothership/internal/ota/autoupdate_test.go simulating a canary quality-degradation event and asserting the rollback OTA command is sent to the canary node's MAC with the previous version/sha256. Verify with: cd ~/spaxel/mothership && go test ./internal/ota/... -v.

issue.close_reason: Verified on real hardware alongside bf-5x46 — persisted-role-matches-assigned-role boot path now arms CSI correctly
issue.description:
Part of ADR-003 / bf-4j97b. Complements bf-5x46 (init ordering) — that fix alone does NOT close this.

In NODE_STATE_CONNECTED, csi_set_role() is reached only inside 'if (bits & SPAXEL_EVENT_ROLE_CHANGED)' (firmware/main/main.c:322-324). That event fires only when the assigned role differs from the persisted one (firmware/main/websocket.c:581).

Observed on hardware 2026-07-30: node persisted role=tx_rx in NVS, fleet optimiser assigned tx_rx, roles equal, no event, CSI dead for the whole boot. Forcing tx_rx -> rx -> tx_rx via /api/nodes/{mac}/role immediately produced 'csi: Setting role', 'wifi:ic_enable_sniffer', 'csi: TX started'.

Why this outlives bf-5x46: once a node persists role=passive, every reboot re-enters CONNECTED with a matching role and never arms CSI again. CSI state must be a function of the node's current role, not of the history of role messages.

Fix: call csi_set_role() unconditionally on entering CONNECTED, keeping the ROLE_CHANGED path for mid-session changes.

Fresh boot on the bench ESP32-S3 reproduced exactly the scenario this bead describes -- NVS persisted role=tx_rx, fleet assigned tx_rx, roles equal, no ROLE_CHANGED event -- and CSI still armed and produced data (mothership /api/links shows 7 live links with real per-link health_details).   go build -o /tmp/spaxel-sim ./cmd/sim
