issue.description:
## Background

Even with good hardware and correct placement, some links will chronically underperform. A user who placed a node on a metal shelf, behind a TV, or in a corner will see consistently poor detection without understanding why. Telling users "your detection quality is low" is useless without telling them what to do about it. Link weather diagnostics provide root-cause analysis and specific, actionable repositioning advice — including 3D visualisation of why a link is performing poorly and where to move a node to fix it.

The name "link weather" is deliberate: just as weather forecasts present complex atmospheric state in human terms ("partly cloudy with 60% chance of rain"), link weather presents complex RF state as: "Node A to Node B: interference detected. Likely cause: microwave oven or 2.4GHz congestion. Try moving Node B 1.5 metres to the right."

## DiagnosticEngine

New module: mothership/internal/diagnostics/linkweather.go

DiagnosticEngine runs as a background goroutine, consuming link health history from SQLite and emitting Diagnosis structs. It runs a full diagnostic pass every 15 minutes.

A Diagnosis struct contains:
- LinkID string
- RuleID string (identifies which rule fired)
- Severity: INFO, WARNING, ACTIONABLE
- Title string (human-readable headline)
- Detail string (explanation of the diagnosis in plain language)
- Advice string (specific actionable steps)
- RepositioningTarget *Vec3 (3D position to move the node to, or nil if repositioning is not the solution)
- RepositioningNodeMAC string (which node to move)
- ConfidenceScore float64 (how confident the diagnostic engine is in this diagnosis)

## Diagnostic Rules

Rule 1: Environmental Change
Trigger: High baseline drift (>5% per hour) correlated across multiple links simultaneously (>50% of active links).
Title: "Environmental change detected"
Detail: "Multiple sensing links are showing simultaneous baseline shifts. This typically indicates a temperature change, or a large object was moved in the space. The system is adapting automatically."
Advice: "No action needed. The baseline will re-stabilise within 30 minutes."
RepositioningTarget: nil
Confidence: 0.85 if drift is correlated across >50% of links

Rule 2: WiFi Congestion or Distance
Trigger: Packet rate health < 0.8 for more than 10 minutes on a single link.
Title: "Node B has low signal rate"
Detail: "Node [B] is only delivering [N]% of the expected [M] packets per second. The most common causes are distance from the WiFi router or congestion from nearby networks."
Advice: "1. Move Node [B] within 10 metres of your WiFi router. 2. If already close, check if the 2.4GHz channel is congested (3+ networks on overlapping channels). 3. ESP32-S3 supports both 2.4GHz and 5GHz — if your router supports 5GHz, update Node B's WiFi config to use the 5GHz SSID."
RepositioningTarget: nil (advice is router proximity, not specific coordinates)

Rule 3: Near-Field Metal Interference
Trigger: Low phase stability (< 0.4) sustained for > 30 minutes during known-quiet periods.
Title: "Metal interference near Node [A]"
Detail: "The sensing link [A to B] has unstable phase measurements even when no one is moving. This is typically caused by metal objects in the near field of the node's antenna (within 10cm): metal shelves, radiators, TV backs, or large appliances."
Advice: "Check for metal objects within 10cm of Node [A]. If Node [A] is on a metal surface or shelf, mount it on a non-metal bracket or wall. Try repositioning it 20-30cm away from metal surfaces."
RepositioningTarget: nil (advice is clearance from metal, not a specific position)

Rule 4: Fresnel Zone Blockage (Half-Room Dead Zone)
Trigger: Consistent miss rate (>30% of test walks that should be detected are missed) in a specific area of the room, AND the missing area correlates geometrically with an obstacle in the link's Fresnel zone.
This rule requires the feedback loop data (Phase 7, spaxel-i28) — specifically the user-submitted false negatives with position information. If no feedback data is available, this rule can trigger heuristically when one side of the room consistently shows lower blob confidence scores.
Title: "Coverage gap detected — possible obstruction"
Detail: "The area near [zone description] shows lower detection coverage. An obstacle may be blocking the path between Node [A] and Node [B], interrupting their sensing zone."
Advice: "Move Node [B] [direction] by approximately [distance] to restore coverage. The target position is marked in green in the 3D view."
RepositioningTarget: computed_optimal_position (see below)

Rule 5: Periodic Interference Spikes
Trigger: Periodic spikes in deltaRMS variance (3-10 events per hour, each lasting 1-3 minutes) not correlated with occupancy data (no people detected moving).
Title: "Periodic interference detected"
Detail: "Node [A] to Node [B] is experiencing regular interference bursts [N] times per hour. This pattern is consistent with a microwave oven, a cordless phone, or a pulsed 2.4GHz source."
Advice: "Consider the following: 1. Is Node [A] or Node [B] near a kitchen? Microwave ovens cause strong 2.4GHz interference. 2. A cordless DECT phone or baby monitor near one of the nodes may be the source. 3. Try moving the affected node at least 2 metres from any 2.4GHz appliances."
RepositioningTarget: nil (interference is appliance-specific)

## Repositioning Advice in 3D

For Rule 4 (Fresnel zone blockage), compute the optimal repositioning target:
1. Use the GDOP-based coverage optimiser from Phase 5 self-healing fleet (spaxel-jc4) to compute the position that maximises GDOP for the blocked zone while keeping all other nodes fixed.
2. The optimal position is the computed_optimal_position Vec3.
3. In the 3D dashboard, render a "ghost" node at this position: translucent version of the node mesh, with a dashed line from the current position to the ghost position.
4. Show expected GDOP improvement: "Moving Node B here would improve detection in the east corner from [N]% to [M]%."

## Weekly Reliability Trends

Store daily health score averages in SQLite: link_health_daily (link_id TEXT, date DATE, avg_health REAL, min_health REAL, max_health REAL, PRIMARY KEY (link_id, date)).

A background job runs daily at midnight and writes the day's health averages from the link health log (link_health_log table: link_id, timestamp, composite_score).

Dashboard shows for each link: 7-day sparkline of daily average health score. "Best day" annotation (highest average) and "worst day" annotation (lowest average). This gives users a sense of long-term reliability.

## Files to Create or Modify

- mothership/internal/diagnostics/linkweather.go: DiagnosticEngine and all 5 rules
- mothership/internal/diagnostics/reposition.go: repositioning target computation
- mothership/internal/health/linkhealth.go: add link_health_log table writes
- dashboard/js/linkhealth.js: link health panel, diagnostics display, ghost node rendering
- mothership/internal/dashboard/routes.go: GET /api/links/{id}/diagnostics, GET /api/links/{id}/health-history

## Tests

- Test Rule 1 (environmental change): inject simultaneous high-drift events across 60% of links, verify diagnosis fires with Severity=INFO
- Test Rule 2 (WiFi congestion): inject packet_rate=0.7 for 15 minutes, verify diagnosis fires with appropriate advice text
- Test Rule 3 (metal interference): inject phase_stability=0.3 for 35 minutes during a quiet window, verify diagnosis fires
- Test Rule 4 (Fresnel blockage): requires feedback data — inject synthetic false-negative feedback events clustered in one spatial zone, verify diagnosis fires and RepositioningTarget is non-nil
- Test Rule 5 (periodic interference): inject 5 deltaRMS variance spikes per hour for 2 hours, verify diagnosis fires with correct periodicity estimate
- Test weekly trend aggregation: inject 7 days of health scores, verify daily averages are correctly computed and stored
- Test that repositioning target is within room bounds and improves GDOP

## Acceptance Criteria

- All 5 diagnostic rules fire correctly on synthetic test data that matches their trigger conditions
- Repositioning advice for Rule 4 appears as a ghost node in the 3D dashboard view
- Expected GDOP improvement shown alongside repositioning ghost node
- Weekly 7-day sparkline visible in link health panel for each link
- Diagnostics accessible via API and displayed in Link Health panel on link click
- Tests pass
issue.title: Link weather diagnostics and repositioning advice

issue.description:
The 0.1.352 Docker image contains firmware compiled with CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE_16MB (16MB header). The fix was already committed in d837598 (sdkconfig.defaults -> 4MB, partitions.csv redesigned for 4MB). But Kaniko served a cached firmware layer for the 0.1.352 build, ignoring the sdkconfig.defaults change.

Symptom: ESP32-S3 (4MB flash) flashed via Web Serial crashes on every boot with:
  spi_flash: Detected size(4096k) smaller than binary image header(16384k). Probe failed.
  assert failed: do_core_init startup.c:326

Fix:
1. In firmware stage of Dockerfile, add a cache-busting ARG before the COPY:
   ARG FIRMWARE_CACHE_BUST=2026-06-03
   This guarantees Kaniko treats the layer as new on the next build.

2. Also add RUN rm -f sdkconfig sdkconfig.old after COPY and before idf.py set-target
   so any stale tracked sdkconfig cannot survive into the build.

After this change, idf.py set-target will regenerate sdkconfig from sdkconfig.defaults
which has CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE_4MB=y, producing firmware with a 4MB header.

Reference: firmware/sdkconfig.defaults (CONFIG_ESPTOOLPY_FLASHSIZE_4MB=y)
           firmware/partitions.csv (4MB layout: factory+ota_0 fit in 4MB)

## Objective
FOURTH (final) child of the bf-39mli split. Record the verified root cause + fix, commit ONLY the files that belong to this bead, and close bf-39mli. This child is deliberately isolated because the final commit/close step is the one most prone to getting stuck on br close failures and re-triggering auto-split.

## Depends on
bf-5mlqh (verified PASS + no regression + reverted unverified changes).

## Reuse (do NOT re-derive)
- Close syntax: br close <id> does NOT accept --body (auto-dispatch templates that say br close --body are WRONG for this br build). Attach the summary as a comment first, then close with no body flag:
  1. br comments add bf-39mli "<summary>"
  2. br close bf-39mli
  3. br sync --flush-only

Split-child 1/4 of the bf-31rd re-split (umbrella bf-31rd). Read-only analysis — NO production code change in this child.

Why this child exists: parent bf-31rd failed 3x partly because it bundled the standard-level analysis with the gcc empirical reality. This child isolates ONLY the C11 7.13.2.1 standard analysis; it does NOT touch the build or gcc.

Scope (firmware/test/test_runner.c, main()'s per-test loop region):
- Identify EVERY automatic (stack/local) variable in scope across the setjmp(g_test_jmp) -> potential longjmp() (fired inside g_tests[i].fn()) -> longjmp-return boundary. [migrated comment from bf-4qk2, 2026-07-04T07:25:20.469651663Z, author cli]
## C11 7.13.2.1 audit — automatic vars across the setjmp/longjmp boundary in main()'s per-test loop

**Child 1/4 of the bf-31rd re-split. Standard-level analysis ONLY.** No file under `firmware/` was modified in this child (verified: `git status` of `firmware/test/test_runner.c` is unchanged by this bead; the existing in-source audit comment at `test_runner.c:308-341` is left untouched). The gcc `-Wclobbered` empirical reality is **out of scope** here — it is child 2's scope. This comment renders only what C11 7.13.2.1 alone says.

### The boundary under audit

`firmware/test/test_runner.c`, `main()`, per-test loop body (lines 239-345):

```c
for (volatile int i = 0; i < g_test_count; i++) {
    printf("RUN: %s\n", g_tests[i].name);
    if (setjmp(g_test_jmp) == 0) {     // <-- setjmp() invocation
        g_tests[i].fn();               // <-- potential longjmp() fires inside here
    }                                  // <-- post-longjmp fall-through path
}
```

The boundary is: the `setjmp(g_test_jmp)` call → a `longjmp()` that fires inside `g_tests[i].fn()` → the longjmp-return path at the `setjmp` call site.

### Enumeration of automatic variables in scope across the boundary

A walk of `main()`'s frame yields exactly **one** automatic object whose scope spans the boundary:

| # | Object | Storage | Scope across boundary? |
|---|--------|---------|------------------------|
| 1 | `i` (`volatile int`, for-init, line 239) | **automatic** (block-scoped) | **YES** — scope is the whole loop body incl. the setjmp call, the body call, and the post-longjmp fall-through |

**Confirmation: NO local passed/failed tallies exist in `main()`.** The only counters/state touched by the recovery flow live outside `main()`'s frame:
- `g_failure_count` — file-scope `static` (line 143), bumped inside `test_record_failure()` (line 170), **not** an automatic of `main()`.
- `g_test_jmp` — file-scope `static` (line 132), **not** an automatic of `main()`.
- `g_tests`, `g_test_count` — file-scope `static` (lines 73-74), not automatics of `main()`.

Both statics have **static storage duration**, so 7.13.2.1 (which speaks only to objects of automatic storage duration) **does not apply to them at all** — their values are unconditionally preserved across `longjmp`. No written/read verdict is required for them under the standard; they are listed only to confirm they are **not** automatics and thus outside the clobber rule's reach. `qsort`/`printf`/`setjmp` arguments are expressions/temporaries, not named automatics, and `qsort` runs before the loop regardless.

### Per-variable verdict — `i`

**The three conjunctive conditions of C11 7.13.2.1p3** (an automatic is indeterminate on longjmp return only if ALL hold): (1) automatic storage duration, local to the function containing the `setjmp`; (2) non-volatile-qualified type; (3) changed between the `setjmp` invocation and the `longjmp` call.

**(a) Written between the `setjmp()` call and a `longjmp()` fired inside the body? — NO.**
The only writes to `i` are the for-init `i = 0` (runs once at loop entry, **before** any `setjmp` call) and the for-increment `i++` (runs at the **end** of each iteration, **after** the body). Within one iteration the order is `setjmp()` → body-or-longjmp-return → end of loop body → `i++`. When a `longjmp` fires inside `g_tests[i].fn()`, control transfers **directly** to the `setjmp` return site; `i++` does **not** execute between the `setjmp()` call and the `longjmp()`. It executes only **after** control has already resumed at the `setjmp` site. Inside the body, `i` is only **read** (to index `g_tests[i]`), never written.

**(b) Read in the post-longjmp path? — YES.**
On longjmp return, `setjmp` yields non-zero, the `if` body is skipped, control falls through to the end of the for-body, where `i++` (reads `i`, then writes) and the `i < g_test_count` re-test (reads `i`) both execute.

**7.13.2.1 conclusion for `i`:** condition (3) — "changed between the `setjmp` invocation and the `longjmp` call" — is **not met** (no write to `i` lands in that window). The conjunctive rule therefore does not bite: **`i` is determinate on the longjmp-return path.** Condition (2) (the `volatile` qualifier on line 239) is consequently **not needed** to keep `i` determinate under the standard — the "changed between setjmp and longjmp" failure alone is sufficient.

### Standard-level conclusion (this child's entire scope)

**Per C11 7.13.2.1 alone, `i` does NOT require `volatile`.** It is determinate on the longjmp-return path purely because it is not changed between the `setjmp()` call and a `longjmp()` fired inside `g_tests[i].fn()` — the for-init runs before `setjmp` and the for-increment runs after the body resumes. No automatic in `main()`'s frame meets all three conjuncts of 7.13.2.1p3, and the only statics in play (`g_failure_count`, `g_test_jmp`) are outside the rule's scope by storage duration.

⚠ **Scope flag:** the above is ONLY the standard-level finding. Whether `volatile` is nevertheless **kept** on `i` to satisfy gcc's `-Wclobbered` (a heuristic warning that does not track the "changed between setjmp and longjmp" distinction) is a separate, empirical/compiler question and is **deliberately deferred to child 2** of this re-split. This child asserts nothing about gcc and changes nothing under `firmware/`.

## C11 7.13.2.1 enumeration — automatics across the setjmp/longjmp boundary in main()'s per-test loop

The boundary under audit:

```

    printf("RUN: %s\n", g_tests[i].name);          // before setjmp, unaffected
    if (setjmp(g_test_jmp) == 0) {                  // <-- setjmp() call
        g_tests[i].fn();                            // <-- longjmp() can fire in here
    }                                               //     (via test_record_failure -> longjmp(g_test_jmp,1))
}                                                   // on longjmp return: fall through if (no else),
```

- (a) Written between the setjmp() call and a longjmp() fired inside the body? **NO — not written.** The only writes to `i` are (1) the for-init `i = 0`, which runs once before the loop and before any in-iteration setjmp, and (2) the for-increment `i++`, which runs AFTER control resumes at the setjmp call site — i.e. after the body has already returned, whether normally or via longjmp. - (b) Read in the post-longjmp path? **YES — read.** On a longjmp return, setjmp yields non-zero, control falls through the `if` (no else body) into the loop continuation, where `i++` reads-and-writes `i` and the `i < g_test_count` condition reads `i`.   - (2) non-volatile — NO (`i` is `volatile`-qualified, which alone exempts it from the indeterminate rule);
  - (3) modified between setjmp() and longjmp() — NO (see (a) above).

- **`g_failure_count` is file-scope `static` (declared outside main(), bumped inside test_record_failure() before the longjmp) — NOT automatic, so 7.13.2.1 does not apply to it at all.**
- **`g_test_jmp` is file-scope `static` — NOT automatic, 7.13.2.1 does not apply.**
- (Likewise `g_tests[]` and `g_test_count` are file-scope statics, not in scope of the rule.)

### Standard-level conclusion
Per C11 7.13.2.1 alone, the sole automatic across the boundary — `i` — is determinate after a longjmp return (it is not modified in the setjmp->longjmp window, and it is volatile-qualified regardless), so **`volatile` is NOT strictly required by the standard.** This is ONLY the standard-level finding: the empirical gcc `-Wclobbered` reality (why `volatile` is kept on `i` anyway) is explicitly child 2's scope and is out of bounds for this child. issue.description:
## Background

The firmware scans BLE advertisements every 5 seconds and relays them to the mothership via the bidirectional protocol (spaxel-o4l, Phase 3). Each BLE relay message contains a list of {mac, name, rssi, manufacturer_data} tuples for all devices heard by that node in the last 5 seconds. Phase 6 turns this raw stream into a structured "People and Devices" registry where users can label their devices and associate them with named people. This is the identity layer that transforms anonymous CSI blobs into "Alice" and "Bob".

## BLE Device Auto-Detection

The mothership can identify device types from manufacturer data embedded in BLE advertisement packets. The Bluetooth SIG assigns Company IDs to manufacturers; the first 2 bytes of manufacturer_data encode the company ID (little-endian).

Company IDs to detect:
- 0x004C (Apple): likely iPhone, iPad, AirPods, or Apple Watch. Sub-type from manufacturer data length and flags.
- 0x0006 (Microsoft): Windows devices
- 0x0075 (Samsung): Samsung phones/tablets
- 0x009E (Fitbit): Fitness trackers
- 0x0157 (Garmin): GPS watches / fitness devices
- 0x0059 (Nordic): Tile trackers (Nordic Semiconductor is used by many Tile-like devices)
- 0x0499 (Ruuvi): Ruuvi temperature/humidity sensors
- 0x00E0 (Google): Android devices (Nearby Share beacons)
Classify all others as "Unknown". The device name field (if present in the advertisement) provides additional signal.

Wearable heuristic: RSSI typically -55 to -75 dBm across multiple nodes with relatively consistent signal (worn close to body). Static devices (speakers, tablets) show higher variance. Flags this heuristic as "possibly wearable" (not definitive).

## BLERegistry

New package: mothership/internal/identity/ble.go

BLERegistry struct: backed by SQLite table ble_devices.

SQLite schema:
CREATE TABLE ble_devices (
  mac TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  name TEXT,
  manufacturer TEXT,
  device_type TEXT,  -- apple_phone, apple_earbuds, fitbit, garmin, tile, samsung, unknown
  label TEXT,        -- user-assigned label
  person_id TEXT,    -- FK to people.id
  rssi_min INTEGER,
  rssi_max INTEGER,
  rssi_avg INTEGER,
  first_seen DATETIME,
  last_seen DATETIME,
  is_archived BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  last_seen_node_mac TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE people (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,  -- uuid
  name TEXT NOT NULL,
  color TEXT,           -- hex colour for dashboard rendering
  created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE person_devices (
  person_id TEXT,
  device_mac TEXT,
  PRIMARY KEY (person_id, device_mac)
);

BLERegistry methods:
- ProcessRelayMessage(nodeMac string, devices []BLEDevice): upsert all devices, update last_seen, update RSSI stats
- GetDevices(includeArchived bool) []BLEDeviceRecord
- UpdateLabel(mac, label string) error
- AssignToPerson(mac, personID string) error
- CreatePerson(name, color string) (Person, error)
- GetPeople() []Person
- ArchiveStale(olderThan time.Duration): set is_archived=true for devices not seen for > olderThan

## BLE MAC Randomisation Handling

Modern iPhones and Android phones randomise their BLE MAC address periodically (every 10-15 minutes for iPhones, similar for Android). This is a fundamental privacy feature. The implications for spaxel:

1. The same physical phone appears as multiple different MAC addresses in the registry. The BLERegistry will create new entries for each rotated address.
2. Long-term tracking of phones by MAC is unreliable. The registry will accumulate many entries for a single phone over time.
3. Workarounds: (a) Apple uses Resolvable Private Addresses (RPA) that can be resolved with the Identity Resolving Key (IRK) — requires pairing, not available without user action. (b) Device name is sometimes consistent across rotations. (c) Wearable devices (Fitbit, Garmin, AirTag) typically do NOT rotate their MACs — they provide reliable long-term tracking.

The dashboard must clearly explain this limitation in the "People and Devices" panel:
"Your phone's Bluetooth address changes regularly for privacy reasons. For reliable person tracking, use a Fitbit, Garmin watch, or AirTag, which have stable addresses."

Grouping heuristic: if two devices have the same manufacturer data prefix (first 6 bytes) and name, and were never seen simultaneously at high RSSI from the same node, they are likely the same device with a rotated MAC. Surface this as a "possible duplicate" suggestion in the UI: "These may be the same device: [mac1] and [mac2]. Merge?"

## REST API

GET /api/ble/devices: returns list of BLEDeviceRecord, optionally filtered by ?archived=true
GET /api/ble/devices/{mac}: returns single device with full history
PUT /api/ble/devices/{mac}: update label, device_type, or person assignment. Body: {"label":"Alice's Phone","device_type":"apple_phone","person_id":"uuid-123"}
DELETE /api/ble/devices/{mac}: archive (not hard delete)

GET /api/people: returns list of People with their associated devices
POST /api/people: create person. Body: {"name":"Alice","color":"#3b82f6"}
PUT /api/people/{id}: update name or color
DELETE /api/people/{id}: soft-delete (retain historical data)

## Dashboard Panel

"People and Devices" sidebar panel showing:
- People section: list of defined people with avatar (initials in circle with their color), device count, last seen time
  - Per person: click to expand, shows associated devices
  - "Add person" button opens inline form
- All devices section (below people): list of devices not yet assigned to a person
  - Per device: device type icon (Apple logo, Fitbit icon, etc.), last seen node (abbreviated), last seen timestamp, RSSI bar
  - Inline label edit on double-click
  - Drag-and-drop to assign to a person card
  - Archive button (hides from active list, accessible via "Show archived" toggle)
- Privacy notice: "Phones may appear multiple times due to address rotation. Wearables and AirTags have stable addresses."

## Tests

- Test device auto-detection: Apple company ID 0x004C -> device_type "apple_phone", Fitbit 0x009E -> "fitbit"
- Test that ProcessRelayMessage correctly upserts devices and updates last_seen and RSSI stats
- Test ArchiveStale marks devices not seen for > 7 days as archived
- Test person creation and device-to-person assignment API calls
- Test MAC randomisation handling: two devices with same name and no simultaneous sighting are flagged as possible duplicates
- Test that archived devices are excluded from GetDevices(false) but included in GetDevices(true)

## Acceptance Criteria

- Discovered BLE devices appear in the dashboard "People and Devices" panel within 30 seconds of first observation
- Device type is auto-detected correctly for Apple, Fitbit, Garmin, and Samsung devices
- User can assign labels and associate devices with named people via the dashboard UI
- Drag-and-drop device-to-person assignment works in the UI
- Devices not seen for > 7 days are automatically archived and hidden from the active list
- Privacy limitation is clearly documented in the panel UI
- Possible duplicate MAC-rotated devices are surfaced as merge suggestions
- Tests pass

issue.description:
Extends bf-26pa. Observed 2026-07-30 and it cost the rest of a bring-up session.

An 'esptool read-flash' aborted with 'A serial exception error occurred: Write timeout', leaving the ESP32-S3 in a state where:
- the USB device stays enumerated (303a:1001, /dev/ttyACM0 present)
- no application runs (no serial output, no WiFi association)
- every subsequent esptool invocation fails with Write timeout, including the --no-stub --before usb-reset flags that flash-chunks.sh uses
- a DTR/RTS toggle via stty hupcl does not recover it

Only a physical USB replug restores it.

This matters well beyond bench convenience: it means the cabled recovery path is NOT dependable even on a node you can reach, which raises the bar for OTA correctness (bf-1447x) and for software self-recovery (safe mode bf-1xywb, watchdog bf-2tgcx) rather than lowering it.

Investigate whether a specific esptool operation/flag combination triggers it, whether a USB port power-cycle (uhubctl or similar) can substitute for a manual replug on the bench rig, and document the recovery procedure in the firmware runbook (bf-26pa).
issue.notes:
Investigation completed 2026-08-15:

## Wedge Condition Confirmed
The ESP32-S3 USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral wedges after failed esptool operations, leaving:
- USB device enumerated (303a:1001, /dev/ttyACM0 present)
- No serial output, no WiFi, no application running
- All subsequent esptool calls fail with 'Write timeout'
- Only physical USB replug recovers it

## Root Cause Identified
- esptool read-flash operations that abort with timeout trigger the wedge
- Chip-side peripheral enters unrecoverable state while USB PHY stays enumerated
- esptool timeout logic cannot detect or recover from this state
- DTR/RTS toggles (stty hupcl) do not reach the peripheral

## Working Solution Found
- '--before usb-reset --after watchdog-reset' causes proper reboot
- '--after hard-reset' is NO-OP on native USB (no bridge wiring RTS/EN)
- '--after no-reset' leaves chip in download mode (appears dead)

## USB Power-Cycle Investigation
- uhubctl: Not available on current system
- PyUSB: Not installed, would require additional setup
- Kernel USB device reset: Untested, may not recover wedged peripheral
- Physical replug remains only guaranteed recovery method

## Documentation Added
Updated docs/notes/recovery-mechanisms.md with comprehensive Layer 3.5:
- Wedge condition symptoms, triggers, and root cause
- Three recovery methods (physical replug, boot window retry, watchdog reset)
- Prevention strategies and flag combinations to avoid
- Future solutions (USB power cycle tools, PyUSB, kernel reset)
- Impact on OTA strategy and recovery checklist

## Flash Script Fixed
Updated scripts/flash-esp32s3.sh to use '--after watchdog-reset' after successful flash:
- Prevents leaving chip in download mode
- Causes USB re-enumeration to confirm recovery
- Reduces wedge occurrences during normal flashing

## Related Beads
- bf-26pa: Original esptool reliability issue (Guru Meditation panics)
- bf-4z6wh: esptool intermittent wedging (confirmed same issue)
- bf-1447x: OTA correctness requirements (raised bar due to wedge)
- bf-1xywb: Safe mode implementation
- bf-2tgcx: Watchdog configuration
issue.title: USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral wedges after a failed esptool operation and needs a physical replug

issue.description:
Child of bf-18yn umbrella. Foundation for giving default spaxel-sim nodes a spread, non-degenerate geometry.

Context: the prior runtime-propagation child (bf-3p6g) wires node PosX/PosY/PosZ into the 3D fusion engine (mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go seeds fusionEngine via fleetReg.GetAllNodes()), and bf-1tsm asserts the result. Scope:
- Add a reusable helper in mothership/internal/simulator that returns spread-out default positions for N nodes across a zone consistent with roomWidth/roomDepth/roomHeight. Reuse/extend CornerPositions/SuggestedNodes in node.go, or add e.g. DefaultNodePositions(space, count) []Point. The standalone cmd/sim/main.go generateNodePositions already does corner placement; align defaults with it.

Acceptance criteria:
- Helper returns N distinct, in-bounds positions; no two nodes co-located; positions span the room (min and max differ on X and Y).

[migrated comment from bf-5lh3j, 2026-08-04T01:34:56.485821636Z, author cli]
Implements ADR-005 (docs/plan/plan.md). Full rationale and design there; summary:

Every ESP32-S3 node is presumed to join the same fleet WiFi network, but wifi_ssid/wifi_pass are currently collected fresh from the user on every single onboarding (dashboard 'Configure WiFi' step -> POST /api/provision request body -> echoed into the provisioning payload). The mothership never stores them. This is what turned today's bench onboarding into a multi-hour ordeal: typing/pasting the real network password into a captive-portal form on every single flash attempt, with no way to avoid it.

Scope:
1. Add SPAXEL_WIFI_SSID / SPAXEL_WIFI_PASSWORD env vars (mothership).
2. POST /api/provision: default wifi_ssid/wifi_pass from that config; keep request-body values as an explicit per-node override (never silently drop the override capability -- some node may legitimately need a different network).
3. Return an error (not a silently-broken provisioning payload) if neither the mothership config nor the request body supplies credentials.
4. Dashboard onboarding wizard: skip the WiFi step entirely when the mothership reports SPAXEL_WIFI_SSID is configured; keep it as an 'Advanced: use a different network' override.
5. Dashboard's captive-portal recovery screen: display the stored credentials in copy-paste-ready form (it cannot submit them automatically -- the browser has no route to the mothership while joined to the device's temporary spaxel-XXXX AP -- see ADR-005 Alternatives Considered for why serial+captive-portal both still need to exist as separate paths).

No firmware changes needed -- this is purely mothership + dashboard, the NVS schema and on-device provisioning protocol are unaffected.

## Objective
Split from parent bf-1yr1w (the --ble matcher check, SECOND link of the bf-2m534 identity chain). `scripts/run-sim-ble-match.sh` currently FAILS: Alice's device IS triangulated (a BLE-only track appears — `blob_id=-1`, `person_name=Alice`, `device_addr=AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:00`) and CSI blobs ARE present (`peak_blobs=2`), but the device never attaches to a real blob, so `GetMatch()` never returns Alice. This child finds the SPECIFIC failing gate — investigation only, NO fix.

## What's already known (reuse, don't re-derive)
- `scripts/run-sim-ble-match.sh` drives the full chain (fixture + sim --ble + /api/ble/matches poll). Run with: `bash scripts/run-sim-ble-match.sh`. At HEAD it prints `FAIL: no real blob match for "Alice"`; final `/api/ble/matches` = `[{"blob_id":-1,"person_name":"Alice","device_addr":"AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:00","confidence":0,"is_ble_only":true}]`.
- The script's own matcher-log grep (`'ble:|identity|triangulat|match'`) MISSES the decisive lines. The matcher prints `[BLEDBG] ...` via stdlib `log.Printf` at `internal/ble/identity.go:427` ("NO blob within 2.0m", with td pos + conf + node count) and `:449-:451` (blob found but `matchConf < MinMatchConfidence`). Capture THOSE.
- Matcher gate constants (`internal/ble/identity.go`): `MaxBLEBlobDistance=2.0` (horizontal X/Z plane only, Y ignored), `MinMatchConfidence=0.6`. Confidence (`identity.go:494`) = `f_observations * f_node_count * f_residual * f_distance` — `confidence=0` means at least one factor is zero.
- The sim RSSI model is ALREADY aligned with the matcher: `cmd/sim/main.go:1145` emits rssi via the matcher's inverse path-loss model and uses the correct `rssi_dbm` key. The script's stale "RSSI model mismatch (-50-20log10(d))" diagnostic is NOT the current cause — do NOT chase it.
- Builds: canonical sim is `mothership/cmd/sim` (has --ble/--verify), NOT the repo-root `cmd/sim/`. 84G free on `/`; no need to clear any target/.

## Scope
- Run `run-sim-ble-match.sh` with the mothership log captured so `[BLEDBG]` lines survive. The script writes `mothership.log` into a mktemp data dir (cleaned on exit) — either re-run with a pinned `DATA_DIR` or tee the mothership output. Grep the full log for `BLEDBG`.
- From the BLEDBG lines, extract for Alice's device: triangulated position (`td.Position`), `NodeCount`, `Confidence`, the nearest CSI blob's position, the horizontal distance to it, and which confidence factor zeroes the product (node count too low? residual huge? no blob within 2m?).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `[BLEDBG]` (or equivalent matcher) log lines captured for Alice's device during a `run-sim-ble-match.sh` run.
- [ ] Identified whether the failing gate is (a) no blob within 2m, OR (b) blob in range but `matchConf < 0.6` — AND which confidence factor (`f_node_count` / `f_residual` / `f_distance` / `f_observations`) is the killer.
- [ ] Root cause stated in ONE sentence, with the supporting numbers (triangulated pos, nearest-blob pos, distance, node count, per-factor confidence).
- [ ] No code fix in this child — diagnosis only.

[migrated comment from bf-6crd7, 2026-07-08T15:04:36.897970660Z, author cli]
## Diagnosis COMPLETE — root cause found (investigation only, no fix)

**Why 3 prior runs found nothing:** `[BLEDBG]` lines are gated behind `bleDebug()` = `os.Getenv("SPAXEL_BLE_DEBUG") != ""` (internal/ble/identity.go:13). The script sets `SPAXEL_LOG_LEVEL=info` but never `SPAXEL_BLE_DEBUG`, so the decisive lines never emit. Re-ran the chain with `SPAXEL_BLE_DEBUG=1` + a persistent DATA_DIR — 75 `[BLEDBG]` lines captured.

**Failing gate: (b) blob in range but matchConf < 0.6.** (An early transient also hits gate (a) — see below.)

Steady-state BLEDBG (Alice / AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:00):
```
[BLEDBG] triangulate readings=4 pos=(3.48,1.52,2.00) conf=0.800 residual=0.138
[BLEDBG] assign blob=5 hDist=1.23m matchConf=0.408 (gate=0.60) tdconf=0.800 nodes=4 resid=0.138   -> REJECTED (0.408 < 0.6)
```
Triangulation converged fine (pos in-room, conf=0.8, 4 nodes, resid=0.138). A CSI blob IS within range (blob 5, hDist=1.23m < MaxBLEBlobDistance=2.0) — but matchConf=0.408 < MinMatchConfidence=0.6, so the device never attaches -> GetMatch() never returns Alice -> BLE-only track (blob_id=-1) persists.

**Per-factor breakdown (computeMatchConfidence, identity.go:494):** matchConf = fObs · fNodes · fResid · fDist
- f_observations = 1.0 (device live)
- f_node_count    = min(1, 0.8+0.05·(4-3)) = 0.85  (4 nodes — good)
- f_residual      = 1 - 0.138/2 = 0.931            (good)
- f_distance      = 1 - (1.23-0.5)/1.5 = 0.513      <- KILLER
- product = 1.0 × 0.85 × 0.931 × 0.513 = 0.408 ✓

**Root cause (one sentence):** A CSI blob IS within range (blob 5, 1.23m < 2m), but matchConfidence=0.408 < 0.6 because the horizontal distance drives f_distance down to ~0.51 — with f_node_count=0.85, f_residual=0.93, f_observations=1.0, the product cannot reach the 0.6 gate; the device sits ~1.23m from the nearest blob (threshold to clear 0.6 is ~0.86m). Even 7 nodes (fNodes->1.0) would still yield 0.478 < 0.6, so distance is the sole blocker.

**Early transient (gate a):** while early readings settle, triangulation briefly blows up to `pos=(-68.64,-68.64,2.00) conf=0.240` (way outside the 5x5x2.5 room) -> `NO blob within 2.0m`. Self-corrects by ~6s to the sane (3.48,1.52) pos; not the standing failure.

**Repro:** `SPAXEL_BLE_DEBUG=1 bash scripts/run-sim-ble-match.sh` (or pin DATA_DIR / tee mothership.log). Log preserved at /tmp/spaxel-bledbg/mothership.log.

**Recommended fix direction (out of scope here — for parent bf-1yr1w):** close the horizontal gap between Alice's BLE-triangulated point and her CSI blob centroid (currently 1.23m; need <0.86m), e.g. co-locate the CSI blob with the walker, or re-examine why blob 5's centroid diverges from the walker position. NOT a matcher-threshold change.

issue.description:
**Implements ADR-002 (`docs/plan/plan.md`).** Serial provisioning is bound to physical UART0, which is not wired to anything on an ESP32-S3 board that exposes only the native USB-Serial/JTAG port. On such boards the dashboard's "Add Node" Web Serial flow cannot provision a node at all.

`firmware/main/provision.c:14` sets `#define PROVISION_UART UART_NUM_0` and the window then does `uart_param_config()` / `uart_driver_install()` / `uart_read_bytes()` / `uart_write_bytes()` against that peripheral (`provision.c:22-124`). UART0 on the ESP32-S3 is GPIO43/44. The validation board (USB ID `303a:1001`, "Espressif USB JTAG/serial debug unit") has no USB-UART bridge — `lsusb` shows no CP210x/CH340 — so GPIO43/44 go nowhere and the host CDC device is the chip's native USB-Serial/JTAG peripheral instead.

Confirmed empirically on hardware. During an open 120 s provisioning window a well-formed payload was written to the host CDC device:

    {"provision":{"ssid":"testnet","password":"...","ms_ip":"192.168.1.50","port":8080}}

The firmware never acknowledged it — no success response, no error response, nothing — and the window subsequently timed out normally:

    I (120495) provision: Provisioning window closed (no provisioning received)

Note also that the `SPAXEL READY <MAC>` handshake banner is emitted with `uart_write_bytes()` (`provision.c:52,64`), so it is *also* invisible on such boards even though the surrounding `ESP_LOGI` lines are visible — the host has no way to detect that a window is open. This is a distinct mechanism from the console-routing sibling bead: routing the ESP_LOG console to USB-Serial/JTAG does **not** fix provisioning, because `uart_write_bytes(UART_NUM_0, ...)` targets the peripheral directly and bypasses console routing entirely.

Scope (per ADR-002 — dual transport):
- Add a USB-Serial/JTAG provisioning transport using the `usb_serial_jtag` driver (`usb_serial_jtag_read_bytes()` / `usb_serial_jtag_write_bytes()`), and listen on it concurrently with UART0 for the duration of the window.
- Emit the `SPAXEL READY <MAC>` banner on **both** transports at the existing 1 Hz cadence, and send the JSON response back on whichever transport the request arrived on.
- Keep the UART0 path working unchanged so bridge-equipped devkits and bare modules wired to a USB-TTL adapter continue to provision.
- Reuse the existing line assembly and JSON parsing — the parser is already covered by host tests (`firmware/test/test_serial_prov.c`); this bead adds a second byte source, it does not re-specify the protocol.
- Guard against double-provisioning if both transports deliver a payload (first complete valid line wins; ignore the rest of the window).

Acceptance criteria:
- On a USB-Serial/JTAG-only ESP32-S3, `SPAXEL READY <MAC>` is observed on the host CDC device once per second while the window is open.
- Sending the provisioning JSON to that device gets a success response and the node reboots provisioned (`provisioned=1` in the NVS config log line on next boot).
- The same firmware still provisions successfully over a USB-UART bridge on UART0 — verify both, do not regress the bridge path.
- Host tests in `firmware/test/` still pass; add coverage for transport selection if any parsing logic is refactored.

Independently reproduced 2026-08-02 via the actual dashboard onboarding wizard end-to-end (not a manual serial payload write) -- same root cause, different angle of confirmation.

Ran the full flow twice on bench (ESP32-S3, 303a:1001, no CP210x/CH340 -- same board class this bead describes): once with placeholder WiFi credentials, once with real ones (#ArdenOne). Both flashes succeeded cleanly. Both provisioning attempts failed identically: 'Waiting for SPAXEL READY signal (up to 30s)...' timed out with zero bytes received on the host CDC device, regardless of credential validity. Confirmed via GET /api/fleet afterward that no node ever registered (nodes: []).

This corroborates the bead's core finding rather than adding a new one: since the JS-side onboard.js wait loop (onboard.js:988-1032) never sees a WiFi-credential-dependent difference in behavior, the failure is fully explained by the UART0/USB-Serial-JTAG mismatch already documented here -- the browser is listening on the right host-side device (WebSerial-selected ttyACM port) but the firmware's uart_write_bytes(UART_NUM_0, ...) banner never reaches it, so nothing the host sends afterward matters. No new information about root cause, just confirms it's 100% reproducible via the real UX path a user would actually take, not just manual esptool/serial testing.

[migrated comment from bf-27ly, 2026-08-07T03:38:38.759437400Z, author cli]
Bench evidence 2026-08-06 (ESP32-S3 50:78:7D:1A:3D:C8, USB-Serial/JTAG only):

RX is confirmed dead, and it is NOT a payload problem. With the provisioning window open, a deliberately invalid line was written to the port and the firmware sent NO reply -- it answers unparseable input unconditionally with {ok:false,error:invalid_json}. TX works fine (the SPAXEL READY beacon arrives), so the board transmits but never receives. Host-side writes complete (333/333 bytes) and NVS read back afterwards was blank (~38 non-zero bytes in 24KB), so nothing was ever parsed.

Likely mechanism: provision.c installs the USB-JTAG driver but never calls esp_vfs_usb_serial_jtag_use_driver(), so the ROM/VFS console path and the driver ISR both drain the same RX FIFO (esp_console_repl.c does make that call). WARNING: adding it alone is NOT a fix -- tried this session, it stalled the beacon loop after one iteration and was reverted.

Working workaround: generate the NVS image with nvs_partition_gen.py (namespace spaxel, schema_ver=1, keys per spaxel.h) and flash it at 0x9000 via scripts/flash-esp32s3.sh. Node then boots provisioned and joins.

Separately fixed this session (commit 1ac2bb7): the beacon used portMAX_DELAY and blocked boot forever before wifi_init() whenever nothing drained the port. See docs/notes/esp32-ota-and-reconnection-handoff.md addendum.

- A header comment block that (a) records the gcc host harness decision from bf-21t (why gcc, not ESP-IDF --target linux), and (b) names the single documented run command that child 3 will make real: 'make -C firmware/test test'.

Acceptance criteria:

First link of the bf-4iewr split. Write the definitive root-cause for the tokenless-sim REJECT failure mode so the remaining children have a precise target. The bead is currently PASSING-BY-ACCIDENT (no reject in a default boot) — this child explains exactly why, and exactly when it breaks.

Confirm and document each of the following against the current source (cite file:line):

## Scope
1. Validator is wired UNCONDITIONALLY: `cmd/mothership/main.go:4494` calls `ingestSrv.SetTokenValidator(provSrv.ValidateToken)` — there is no config/build gate, so "validator configured?" is always YES.
2. The validator reads `hello.Token` only: `internal/ingestion/server.go:513` (`tokenOK := hello.Token != "" && validator(hello.MAC, hello.Token)`).
3. The sim sends its provisioned token ONLY as the `X-Spaxel-Token` HTTP header (`cmd/sim/main.go:633`, also `cmd/sim/scenario.go:318`) and does NOT include a `token` field in the hello JSON body (hello map at cmd/sim/main.go ~640).
4. The mothership NEVER reads that header — `grep -rn 'X-Spaxel-Token\|Header.Get' cmd/mothership/ internal/` returns no WS-path hit. Consequence: `hello.Token` is always "" for sim nodes → `tokenOK` always false → the "supply valid tokens" option in the parent bead is currently NON-FUNCTIONAL.
5. The only thing accepting sim nodes is the migration window: `internal/ingestion/server.go:515`. MigrationWindowHours DEFAULTS TO 24 (`internal/config/config.go:139`), so a fresh boot opens a 24h window → sim nodes accepted as Unpaired, no reject (matches PROGRESS.md bf-3hji).
6. Therefore REJECT fires ONLY when the window is closed: `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0` (deadline never set -> IsZero() -> reject branch), OR uptime > 24h. In those cases every sim node logs "missing token" -> sendReject(conn, "invalid_token") -> disconnect.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A written root-cause finding posted as a comment on bf-4iewr, confirming points 1-6 with file:line citations.
- [ ] Explicit statement that current "no reject" is a 24h-window MASK, not a real fix.
- [ ] Explicit statement that the token-supply path is currently dead (header ignored, hello.Token empty).

issue.description:
docs/plan/plan.md Component 30 Spatial Context Notifications (~line 2075-2093) specifies an 8-step render pipeline for the notification thumbnail image via github.com/fogleman/gg, with step 2 being: "if floor plan image exists: draw as background, resized to fit".

mothership/internal/notify/service.go GenerateFloorPlanThumbnail() (~line 608-640) implements steps 1 and 3+ (dark background fill, blob circles, etc.) but step 2 is a literal no-op:

    // Draw floor plan if available
    // TODO: decode and draw floor plan image background
    _ = floorPlan // Used when TODO is implemented

The floorPlan bytes are fetched from s.floorPlan under lock but then explicitly discarded. This means every push/webhook notification image (fall alerts, zone-entry, security-motion, anomaly -- Component 30 table ~line 2093-2100) renders blobs on a flat dark-gray background instead of over the user's actual uploaded floor plan (the floor plan upload/calibration feature itself, spaxel-6hd, is already closed and working -- this is specifically the notification-renderer half not consuming it). This degrades the "spatial context" the feature is named for -- a user glancing at a phone notification sees dots on a blank rectangle instead of a recognizable room layout.

No open or in-progress bead currently tracks this (confirmed via bf search for "floor plan image" -- only the unrelated closed dashboard-upload bead spaxel-6hd matched).

Fix: in GenerateFloorPlanThumbnail, decode floorPlan (PNG bytes, same format/source as the dashboard 3D ground-plane texture from spaxel-6hd -- see mothership/internal/floorplan or wherever GET /api/floorplan/image reads from) via Go's image/png, scale/resize to fit the width x height canvas using the same scaleX/scaleZ transform already computed for blob positions, and draw it as the background layer before the zone/blob layers (matching plan.md's specified render order and the "Background layer is cached" performance note ~line 2082 -- consider caching the decoded+resized image keyed on floor plan content hash, since this function is documented to target <50ms). Add a test in mothership/internal/notify covering: with a floor plan image set, the output PNG's background pixels differ from the flat #1a1a1a fill; with no floor plan set, behavior is unchanged (existing flat-fill path). Verify with: cd mothership && go test ./internal/notify/... -run FloorPlanThumbnail -v.

issue.description:
Split-child 2 of 3 for parent bf-1na (Add main() entry-point skeleton with setjmp recovery loop and run-command header). Builds on child 1 (bf-1zew, which added the run-command comment + the naive registry iteration that calls each g_tests[i].fn() directly). This child is the core contract of bf-1na: make a failing assertion non-fatal by driving each test through the per-test setjmp/longjmp recovery loop.

Scope (extend firmware/test/test_runner.c):
- In main()'s per-test loop, before calling the body, setjmp(g_test_jmp) — the file-scope jmp_buf from sibling bf-3id. Evaluate its return: on the DIRECT call setjmp returns 0 and the body runs normally; if a failed assertion inside the body calls test_record_failure(), that longjmp(g_test_jmp, 1) returns control to the setjmp call site with a non-zero value instead.
- On the non-zero (longjmp) return, do NOT re-invoke the body — just fall through to advance the loop. On the 0 return, call g_tests[i].fn() as before.
- Either way the loop advances to i+1, so a failure in test N never blocks tests N+1..end. That per-test isolation is the whole point.
- Keep printing one observable line per test BEFORE the setjmp (e.g. the RUN: line from child 1) so that, when a test fails, the lines for the tests after it still appear — which is how this child's acceptance is verified. (Outcome-based PASS/FAIL labels land in child 3; do not add them here.)

Implementation note (the classic setjmp trap): any automatic variable that is modified between setjmp and longjmp AND read after the longjmp returns must be volatile-qualified, else its value is indeterminate (C11 7.13.2.1). The loop index i is read in the post-longjmp path — confirm it is not modified between the setjmp call and the longjmp (it is only incremented by the for-loop increment, which runs AFTER control returns), so no volatile is needed; double-check this holds for the structure you write.

Acceptance criteria:
- main() setjmp()s into g_test_jmp before each test and calls the body only on the 0 return; on a longjmp return it advances without re-calling.
- A failing assertion in one test does NOT prevent later tests from running — verifiable by temporarily adding an intentionally-failing TEST() followed by a passing TEST() and confirming both tests' per-test lines print and the process completes (rather than aborting) when run via `make -C firmware/test test`.
- Compiles cleanly with gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra (no setjmp-related warnings).
- No changes to firmware/main/* or firmware/CMakeLists.txt.
issue.title: Wrap each test in per-test setjmp/longjmp recovery so a failing assertion is non-fatal

A node could OTA into a build whose CSI pipeline is completely dead and still mark itself valid, cancelling the rollback that would have saved it. issue.description:
## Goal
When system detects that user might be struggling or detection quality has degraded, proactively offer contextual help — but never when things are working well.

## Trigger conditions and responses:

Detection quality drops:
- Condition: Zone-level detection quality below 60% for >24 hours
- Banner in timeline and 3D view: 'Detection in the kitchen has been less reliable this week. Want me to help diagnose?'
- Guided flow: Check node connectivity → show link health with explainability → suggest node repositioning → offer re-baseline → 'Still not right? Try adding a node here [highlighted position]'

Repeated setting changes:
- Condition: Same settings key modified 3+ times within 60-minute sliding window (qualifying keys: delta_rms_threshold, breathing_sensitivity, tau_s, fresnel_decay, n_subcarriers)
- Tracking: per-key edit counter in memory, resets after 60 min inactivity
- Trigger: when counter reaches 3, set hint_pending flag
- Frontend: show non-intrusive banner: 'You've adjusted the detection threshold several times. Would you like me to show you what the system is seeing?' with [Show me] and [×] dismiss
- [Show me]: opens time-travel to most recent detection event before first edit, with explainability overlay pre-activated
- Cooldown: 24 hours after hint is shown

Node offline:
- Condition: Any node offline for >2 hours
- Timeline event with expandable troubleshooting steps

First-time feature discovery:
- Condition: User opens feature panel for first time
- Brief, non-intrusive tooltip (not modal): 'Draw a box around an area, then choose what happens when someone enters or leaves. [Got it]'
- Shown once, never repeated

After false positive feedback:
- Inline response in timeline: 'Got it. I've slightly raised the detection threshold for the contributing links. If this keeps happening at this time of day, my hourly baseline will adapt within a few days.'

After successful calibration:
- Positive reinforcement: 'Re-baseline complete. Detection quality in the kitchen improved from 64% to 89%.'

## Design principles
- Reactive, not proactive: help appears only when something seems wrong or when user is clearly exploring
- Dismissible in one tap: never blocks UI
- Never repeats after dismissal (stored in localStorage)
- Always explains what will happen next
- Never condescending: assumes user is intelligent but may not know CSI physics

## Acceptance
- Detection quality drop triggers helpful banner
- Repeated setting changes trigger hint
- Node offline shows troubleshooting steps
- First-time feature discovery shows tooltip once
- Feedback responses are helpful
- Calibration success shows positive reinforcement

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x. MUST be fixed before any node is distributed — fixing it later requires physically reflashing every node.

firmware/partitions.csv:
  factory,  app,  factory, 0x10000, 0x1F0000,
  ota_0,    app,  ota_0,   0x200000,0x1F0000,
  otadata,  data, ota,     0x3F0000,0x2000,

with the comment 'Single OTA partition for A/B updates with rollback'. That is not what this layout does.

esp_ota_get_next_update_partition() cycles among OTA partitions ONLY — 'factory' is not one. With exactly one OTA partition:
- running from factory -> next is ota_0 -> first OTA succeeds (verified on hardware 2026-07-30, factory 0x10000 -> ota_0 0x200000)
- running from ota_0   -> next is ota_0 -> esp_ota_begin() rejects writing the running partition with ESP_ERR_OTA_PARTITION_CONFLICT

So every node gets exactly one OTA, then can never be updated again without serial access. The bench node is now ON ota_0, i.e. already spent its single update.

Worse, firmware/main/websocket.c maps every esp_ota_begin failure to the generic status 'write_failed', so this presents as a mysterious write error rather than a layout problem.

Fix:
- move to a true A/B layout (ota_0 + ota_1, dropping or shrinking factory) within the 4MB budget
- surface ESP_ERR_OTA_PARTITION_CONFLICT as its own OTA status instead of 'write_failed'
- VERIFY by running two consecutive OTAs on one node

Note the layout change is itself breaking: nodes flashed with the current table need a serial reflash to adopt it. That is exactly why this must land before distribution.
issue.notes:
[migrated comment from bf-436bh, 2026-07-30T21:25:02.902762359Z, author cli]
Concrete A/B layout for indefinite OTA (4MB flash).

REQUIREMENT: two OTA-type partitions. esp_ota_get_next_update_partition alternates ota_0 <-> ota_1 forever. 'factory' can never be an OTA target, which is why the current table caps at one update.

Proposed partitions.csv (4MB, nvs/phy_init offsets UNCHANGED so provisioning survives):

  nvs,      data, nvs,     0x9000,  0x6000,
  phy_init, data, phy,     0xF000,  0x1000,
  otadata,  data, ota,     0x10000, 0x2000,
  ota_0,    app,  ota_0,   0x20000, 0x1F0000,
  ota_1,    app,  ota_1,   0x210000,0x1F0000,

Both app offsets are 64KiB-aligned (0x20000, 0x210000) and ota_1 ends exactly at 0x400000.
Slot size 0x1F0000 = 2,031,616 B. Current binary 1,623,392 B => 79.9% full, ~408 KiB headroom.

TRADE-OFF: 4MB cannot hold A/B *and* a factory recovery image (3 x ~1.55MiB > 4MiB). Dropping factory is the standard A/B product choice; if both slots are ever bad, recovery is serial. Bootloader rollback covers the common case.

HEADROOM WARNING: ~408 KiB is not much. Enabling HTTPS on the OTA client and/or signed-app verification (bf-1uefm) will consume a large fraction of it. If signed OTA is wanted, evaluate an 8MB/16MB module for future hardware before committing to 4MB.

MIGRATION: a partition-table change cannot be applied over OTA — it needs serial flash of bootloader (0x0), partition table (0x8000), and the app slots. BUT because nvs stays at 0x9000/0x6000, flashing those regions WITHOUT erase-flash preserves NVS, so nodes keep their WiFi credentials and provisioned flag and do not need re-provisioning.

UNCONFIRMED: physical flash capacity. The 4MiB backup was dumped with esptool --flash-size 4MB, which does not prove the chip is 4MB, and sdkconfig.defaults hedges 'Safe on 16MB boards'. Run 'esptool flash-id' on a node to confirm before finalising the table — if the modules are 16MB, slots can be far more generous and the HTTPS/signing tension disappears.

[migrated comment from bf-436bh, 2026-07-30T21:30:59.658246736Z, author cli]
CORRECTION to the migration note above: a partition-table change CAN be applied over OTA, contrary to what was stated. The WLED ecosystem does exactly this (softplus/Esp32Repartition, johnmu.com/2024-esp32-partition-update): OTA a small purpose-built firmware whose only job is to rewrite the partition table in place — find the 0xAA50 magic at 0x8000/0x9000, parse, resize, recalc MD5, erase and rewrite. The critical write window is ~100ms and modern bootloaders verify the MD5, so a corrupt table refuses to boot rather than booting garbage.

BUT it does not rescue spaxel's nodes, for a sequencing reason that matters:

- the technique requires the device to be running from the FIRST app partition so both slots can be safely resized
- the published tool only supports an app0/app1/data layout, which is not spaxel's factory+ota_0
- most importantly: each spaxel node has exactly ONE OTA available. A node still on 'factory' could spend that single update on a repartition firmware and recover remotely. A node already moved to ota_0 CANNOT receive any further OTA at all, so it can only be recovered over serial.

The bench node is already on ota_0 and is therefore already in the unrecoverable-remotely state.

Practical consequence: 'fix before distribution' still holds, but the reason is sharper. It is not that remote repartitioning is impossible — it is that the one available OTA per node is the only chance to do it, and it is spent the moment a node takes any other update.

issue.description:
ADR-007 phase 1, mothership side. Sibling work: firmware (bf-59b07) and dashboard -- none of the three is useful alone.

Today node identity is a static credential derived as HMAC-SHA256 over the install key and the mac, so ONE install key mints a valid credential for ANY mac. Replace it with a per-device value the browser generates at flashing time.

Add two endpoints:
 - POST /api/nodes/{mac}/enroll -- body carries the browser-generated 256-bit device key as 64 hex chars. Stores it against the mac in state registered. Operator-authenticated: a browser-to-mothership call, behind the dashboard existing forward-auth (Google SSO). Deliberately the INVERSE of /firmware (ADR-006), which must be node-authenticated. Do NOT invent a new auth mechanism for either.
 - POST /api/nodes/{mac}/enroll/activate -- flips registered to active once the browser confirms the device stored it.

Storage columns: mac, device key, state, efuse_block_index (nullable), enrolled_at. efuse_block_index is unused in phase 1 but should exist now -- ADR-007 phase 2 records which of the six eFuse key blocks a device consumed, and adding it later means migrating a table that by then holds fleet data.

Challenge-response on the ingestion handshake:
 - Mothership sends a nonce on connect; node returns HMAC-SHA256 over the device key and that nonce; verify with constant-time compare (crypto/subtle, as provisioning.ValidateToken already does).
 - The device key is NEVER transmitted after enrollment. That is what removes replay, and replay matters immediately because LAN nodes speak plain ws:// by design (ADR-006 decision 6).

Compatibility: the existing static-token path and the migration window setting must keep working during phase 1, so unenrolled nodes are not locked out mid-migration. Retire the old path only when every node is active.

Acceptance: an enrolled node connects by answering a nonce challenge and never sends its key; a replayed response from a previous connection is rejected; an unenrolled node still connects via the existing path.

issue.description:
Part of ADR-004 / bf-1447x. Prior art: ESPHome's safe_mode component (esphome.io/components/safe_mode).

Bootloader rollback only catches an image that FAILS TO BOOT. It does nothing for the more common and more dangerous case: an image that boots, connects, and is broken. Spaxel's health gate makes this worse — it marks the slot valid on the first role message (bf-5vwo8), so a broken build actively cancels its own rollback.

ESPHome's answer needs no extra partition and no flash budget:
- count consecutive boot failures (counter in RTC memory or flash)
- a boot only counts as good after the device stays up for boot_is_good_after (default 1 minute)
- after num_attempts failures (default 10), boot into safe mode: EVERYTHING disabled except serial logging, network, and OTA
- reboot_timeout (default 5 min) so it does not sit in safe mode forever

That converts 'soft-bricked node behind a wall' into 'node that is still reachable for another OTA'. For spaxel this is arguably higher value than a third partition, because it costs no flash.

INTERACTION WARNING (bf-2tgcx): ESPHome 2026.4.0 shipped a regression where the Task Watchdog reset devices before the 60-second boot-validation window closed, spuriously triggering OTA rollback (esphome/esphome#15767, emporia-vue-local discussion #409). Spaxel has the same shape — a 60s role-message validation window — and is about to enable the watchdog. Choose the watchdog timeout and the validation window together, not independently.

bf-16tsv diagnosis — VERDICT (b): /ws/dashboard frames carry NO blobs. Defect is mothership emission, NOT downstream render/probe.

== Runtime evidence (identity-less sim, 4 nodes / 3 walkers / rate 30 / seed 42, 12s raw-WS capture) ==
Tool: docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/capture-ws-frames.mjs (v3, binary-vs-text aware; v2 conflated raw CSI binary frames into the JSON "<no-type>" bucket). Artifact: docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/identity-less.ws-frames.json.

Frame census over the capture window:
- binary_frames=4368  (opcode 0x2 — raw CSI broadcast by hub.BroadcastCSI; not JSON, cannot carry blob objects)
- text_frames=241     (opcode 0x1 JSON): snapshot=1, event=98, <no-type>(10Hz delta ticks)=120, motion_state=22
- text_frames_carrying_blobs=0   <-- ZERO of 241 JSON frames contain a "blobs" array at any nesting level (blob_field_census is empty)

Meanwhile, at the SAME instant, /api/blobs returns 2 blobs with positions/ids:
  GET /api/blobs -> [{"ID":1,"X":4.7,"Y":0.3,"Z":1.9,...,"Weight":0.82,"identityResolved":false},
                     {"ID":2,"X":4.7,"Y":0.3,"Z":2.1,...,"Weight":0.82}]   (peak count=2, seen in 8/24 polls)

Sample 10Hz delta-tick frame (the frames the dashboard blob renderer is supposed to read) — note it has "events" but NO "blobs":
  {"events":[{"blob_id":0,"id":"presence:...","kind":"presence_transition",...}, ...], "timestamp_ms":...}
  -> delta frames omit "type" (by design, hub.go:734) and carry "events"/"nodes"/"links"/"motion_states" but never "blobs".

The snapshot frame (4785 chars) likewise has NO top-level "blobs" key — only links/motion_states/nodes.

N.B. the dashboard console DOES flood with "detection ... blob #N" lines because typed "event" frames (kind:"detection") ARE emitted and carry x/y/z in detail_json — but those are event notifications, not the live "blobs" array the render path consumes. That is exactly why the console is noisy yet renderEvidence blobCount=0.

== Root cause (code-level, deterministic) ==
The dashboard hub has exactly ONE path that puts blobs into the WS feed: Hub.BroadcastLocUpdate() (mothership/internal/dashboard/hub.go:564), which is the sole writer of h.snap.blobsJSON. That cache is read by BOTH emitters:
  - buildSnapshot()  hub.go:687-693   -> snap["blobs"] only if blobsJSON non-empty
  - tickDelta()      hub.go:797-799   -> delta["blobs"] only if blobsJSON non-empty
BroadcastLocUpdate has ZERO callers (grep across mothership/ — only its own definition + 2 comments). So blobsJSON is never populated, so neither the snapshot nor any 10Hz delta ever carries blobs.

The blobs DO exist in-process: the 10Hz fusion loop (mothership/cmd/mothership/main.go:2135-2137) computes blobs and publishes them via pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs); /api/blobs (main.go:4377) reads pm.GetTrackedBlobs() directly — a completely separate path that bypasses the dashboard hub. Nothing ever bridges SetTrackedBlobs -> BroadcastLocUpdate.

== Implication for bf-4gd4j ==
This bead isolates the layer: emission is the defect. bf-4gd4j's "apply a fix" should wire the fusion loop to call dashboardHub.BroadcastLocUpdate(trackedBlobs) on each 10Hz tick (converting []TrackedBlob -> []tracking.Blob as BroadcastLocUpdate expects), so blobsJSON is populated and the snapshot+delta frames carry blobs. A config/seed bump (SIM_DURATION/SIM_SEED/blob-timeout) CANNOT fix blobSeen — the data simply never reaches the browser. (Diagnosis only here; no code change in bf-16tsv.)

## bf-16tsv — /ws/dashboard blob emission: VERDICT (b), no blobs emitted

Diagnostic bead (1 of 4 splitting bf-4gd4j). Captured RAW /ws/dashboard frames during an identity-less sim (4 nodes / 3 walkers / rate 30 / seed 42, no --ble) and compared to /api/blobs at the same instant.

**VERDICT: (b) — the WS feed carries NO blobs. The defect is mothership EMISSION, not downstream render/probe.**

### Runtime evidence
Capture tool: `docs/notes/bf-4do5y-runtime-capture/capture-ws-frames.mjs` (v3, binary-vs-text aware, direct ws client on SIM_PORT 8088, 12 s window). Full output: `identity-less.ws-frames.json`.

- 4368 binary frames (raw CSI via BroadcastCSI) + 241 JSON text frames captured
- **0 / 241** JSON text frames carry a `blobs` array — including the very first `snapshot` frame and all 120 `<no-type>` delta ticks (10 Hz × 12 s)
- type histogram (text): `{snapshot:1, event:98, <no-type>:120, motion_state:22}`
- `blob_field_census: {}` (no frame anywhere has a top-level `blobs` key)
- At the same instant, `/api/blobs` returns **2 blobs** with positions/ids (api_peak_blob_count=2; 8/24 api samples had blobs)

### Sample frame excerpt (snapshot — the first message on connect)
The snapshot carries `links`, `motion_states` (several motion_detected:true, delta_rms up to ~6.5), `nodes` (4 sim nodes), `zones:[]`, `timestamp_ms`, `type:"snapshot"` — and **no `blobs` field at all**:
```
{"links":[...12...],"motion_states":[{...,"motion_detected":true,"delta_rms":6.55...},...],
 "nodes":[4 sim ESP32-S3],"timestamp_ms":1785048619486,"type":"snapshot","zones":[]}
```
Compare `/api/blobs` at t=1785048619488 (same instant):
```
[{"ID":1,"X":4.7,"Y":0.3,"Z":1.9,"VX":0,"Weight":0.82,"identityResolved":false}, ...count:2]
```
The console "detection events by blob #N" flood is real — those are the 98 `event` frames emitted by `eventsHandler.LogEvent("detection",...)` in the tracker goroutine. They carry blob_id in `event.detail_json` but are not blob render data.

### Root cause (code-level, deterministic)
`Hub.BroadcastLocUpdate(blobs)` — `internal/dashboard/hub.go:566` — is the **sole writer** of `h.snap.blobsJSON`, which both `buildSnapshot()` (hub.go:797) and `tickDelta()` (hub.go:688) read to populate the `blobs` field/key. **`BroadcastLocUpdate` has ZERO callers in the entire codebase** (`grep -rn '.BroadcastLocUpdate('` → empty).

The live tracker goroutine (`cmd/mothership/main.go` ~2110-2200, 10 Hz) does:
1. `fusionEngine.Fuse(...)` → peaks
2. `blobTracker.track(result)` → blobs
3. `pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs)` ← ONLY publish path → feeds `/api/blobs` + `/api/tracks` (why those return 2 blobs)
4. `eventsHandler.LogEvent("detection",...)` ← the console flood
5. identity matcher update + write-back

It never bridges blobs into the dashboard hub. The `BlobBroadcaster` interface that `BroadcastLocUpdate` satisfies is wired **only** to the replay handler (`replayHandler.SetBlobBroadcaster(dashboardHub)`, main.go:1784), never the live tracker.

Net: `/api/blobs` independently returns live blobs; `/ws/dashboard` snapshot+delta both read an eternally-empty `blobsJSON`. Downstream render/probe code is exonerated — there is nothing on the wire for it to render.

### Fix location (for the fix bead, not this one)
In the tracker goroutine after `pm.SetTrackedBlobs(blobs)`, add `dashboardHub.BroadcastLocUpdate(toTrackingBlobs(blobs))` (the hub expects `[]tracking.Blob`; TrackedBlob → tracking.Blob conversion needed), guarded by `dashboardHub != nil`. No code change made in this diagnosis-only bead.

issue.description:
Second link of the bf-4iewr split (depends on the root-cause finding). The token the sim provisions never reaches the validator — make the token path REAL so a sim node presenting a valid token is accepted even when the migration window is closed.

## Problem (confirmed by the root-cause child)
- Validator reads only `hello.Token` (`internal/ingestion/server.go:513`).
- Sim sends its token only as the `X-Spaxel-Token` HTTP header (`cmd/sim/main.go:633`), never in the hello body, and the mothership never reads that header. So `hello.Token` is always "" and every node falls through to the migration-window branch.

## Scope
Pick ONE bridging approach and implement it (justify the choice in the PR/comment):
- (A) Server-side: in the `/ws/node` upgrade handler, read `X-Spaxel-Token` from the WS handshake request and inject it into the parsed hello (`nc.Hello.Token` / the value passed to the validator) before the validation check at server.go:506-530; OR
- (B) Client-side: have the sim include a `"token"` field in the hello JSON body (`cmd/sim/main.go` hello map ~640, and `cmd/sim/scenario.go`).

Prefer the option that keeps real ESP32 firmware behavior unchanged (firmware today sends token in hello — verify against `firmware/main/websocket.c`). Do not weaken the validator.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A node presenting a VALID provisioned token is accepted and marked paired (not Unpaired) even when `SPAXEL_MIGRATION_WINDOW_HOURS=0` (window closed) — proven by a test.
- [ ] A node presenting an INVALID/empty token is still REJECTED when the window is closed (regression guard; do not break rejection).
- [ ] Test (unit or e2e) exercises the bridge end-to-end through `ValidateToken` (`internal/provisioning/server.go:135`, HMAC-SHA256(installSecret, mac)).

issue.description:
Root-caused the 'post-reflash silence' / 'device did not become ready after
flashing' failure that blocked ESP32-S3 onboarding, via direct serial/USB
debugging on bench (dozens of BOOT/RST/power-cycle cycles, usbmon capture).
Three compounding issues, all fixed:

1. firmware/main/provision.c listened on physical UART0 (GPIO43/44) for the
   provisioning handshake, but this board has no USB-UART bridge chip --
   only native USB-Serial-JTAG. Boot logs worked (console correctly routed
   per sdkconfig.defaults), but the provisioning listener's UART0 traffic
   went nowhere. Fixed: switched to the usb_serial_jtag driver (same
   peripheral console/esp_log already uses), following the install pattern
   from ESP-IDF's own esp_console_repl.c.

2. Dockerfile's firmware merge_bin step wrote the app to 0x10000, which was
   correct under the OLD partition table but became the `otadata` partition
   after the 2026-07-30 true-A/B migration (ADR-004/bf-436bh) moved app
   slots to 0x20000/0x210000. Every wizard reflash was silently corrupting
   otadata (and the start of ota_0) while the bootloader kept booting
   whatever old image happened to already be in an OTA slot -- explains why
   reflashing never seemed to change behavior. Fixed: merge now includes
   ota_data_initial.bin at 0x10000 and places the app at 0x20000, matching
   `idf.py build`'s own suggested flash-args for the current partitions.csv.

3. Even with both fixes, the native USB-Serial-JTAG RX path is intermittently
   unreliable at the USB level -- confirmed via usbmon that a bulk OUT
   transfer can be submitted by the host and never acknowledged by the
   device, while the SAME device's TX (SPAXEL READY broadcasts, esp_log) is
   100% reliable every time. This looks like an ESP32-S3 silicon/driver
   errata, not an application bug -- the ESP-IDF usb_serial_jtag driver's
   install/ISR code was reviewed and matches the reference implementation.
   Mitigated rather than fixed: dashboard/js/onboard.js now (a) retries the
   provisioning JSON write up to 5x, and (b) no longer treats a missing
   serial ack as fatal -- only an explicit {"ok":false,...} response is.
   Real confirmation of success now comes from the existing detect_node step
   polling /api/nodes for the node to appear online over WiFi, which is
   strictly stronger proof than a serial ack (the device can only do that
   with working credentials actually written to NVS).

Verified end-to-end on bench: fixed firmware boots today's build (not a
stale cached image), broadcasts SPAXEL READY reliably, and a clean
single-shot write after a full power-cycle succeeds at the USB level.
issue.title: Onboarding wizard 'device did not become ready' -- root-caused to 3 compounding bugs, fixed
